The US and Iran trade missile barrages as hopes dim for a quick resolution

The United States and Iran each fired barrages of missiles Thursday, as the pattern of back-and-forth strikes took hold again and hope dimmed for any quick resolution.

After a brief respite, the risk of a return to all-out war emerged once more, with the fighting threatening to engulf even more countries: Jordan said Thursday it intercepted Iranian missiles for the second consecutive day, while Kuwait said a strike in the northern part of the country killed one person. Also this week, drones caused fires on ships at an Egyptian port, and Saudi Arabia said it came under fire from Iran-backed militias in Iraq.

The spiraling violence underscored the difficulty of winding down a five-month conflict that has sent the price of fuel and other basics soaring, jolted the world economy, and added to concerns about American stockpiles of weapons needed to defend its bases and allies. After an earlier hiatus had given hope that diplomatic efforts were moving forward, there was no public sign of progress.

News.title: 5% savings accounts are finally back – here’s where to get the best deals
News.content:
Higher interest rates have been a burden for homeowners and businesses over the past couple of years – but they have also been a real boost for people with savings.

Even while inflation has remained between 2.6 and 3.8 per cent over the past year, savings accounts have offered an even higher rate of interest to ensure both that your money grows, but also importantly, grows at a faster pace than prices are rising.

Inflation erodes the buying power of cash, but as long as savers have been happy to move their cash, a raft of banks, building societies and finance apps have offered consistently above 4 per cent - and now, as expectations grow that the Bank of England may raise the base rate, an even higher benchmark has been set.

Yes, the 5 per cent interest savings account has made a return.

It’s certainly not everywhere, with Moneyfacts data showing that on 30 July, the average easy access savings rate was just 2.56 per cent.

And the biggest names are still offering a woefully low rate for the most part; in fact, research by savings app Spring showed that high street banks were still offering a dismal average of 0.96 per cent interest last month, on restriction-free easy access accounts.

But for savers willing to move their cash, options are there to earn £50 a year on each £1,000 in a savings pot – but it’s important to know that not all accounts are created equally, and each has their own drawbacks and benefits to consider beyond the headline rate.

open image in gallery ( Getty Images/iStockphoto )

Revolut, for example, is offering 5 per cent - but that rate only lasts until 4 December of this year. Still a good short-term boost, of course, but it’s also only available to new customers and if you open an account before 4 August. From early December, that rate returns to 2.9 per cent if you are on a standard plan, or higher if you pay for premium tiers.

Lemfi, a financial services company originally set up to help immigrants move or send money, is also offering 5 per cent for six months, which then lowers to 3.04 per cent. Cash with them is held by ClearBank, an FSCS-protected and regulated bank.

And Cahoot, which is owned by Santander, have a Sunny Day Saver which pays 5 per cent too - theirs lasts for a full 12 months, but is only for balances up to £3,000. No interest is paid above that threshold, making it ideal for savers with smaller tallies to begin with.

Santander are one of the banks offering even higher - 6 per cent in their Edge Saver - but that, and others, are for clients who have paid-for current accounts, which can similarly hold restrictions on amounts or number of withdrawals allowed.





The milestone interest rate hasn’t hit the Cash ISA market just yet, with the best offering around the 4.6 per cent mark so far, but fixed term accounts are firmly in the 5 per cent territory too - for the first time in two years.

Investec launched their three-year saver this week, guaranteeing 5 per cent annually for balances of between £5,000 and £250,000 - and paying out that interest each year, so you don’t end up with a three-year lump at once, which could generate a tax bill. However, the trade-off with fixed-term bonds is that you lock your money away for the whole period.

Atom Bank has also hit 5 per cent, though that’s for an even longer five-year term; great if you want certainty over earnings, though for periods above three years, most finance experts suggest considering whether you should invest a portion of your money as that can generate higher returns than savings over longer periods.

Caitlyn Eastell, personal finance analyst at Moneyfactscompare.co.uk, said: “For the first time since 2024, the market-leading fixed bond now pays a 5 per cent return. For someone with £20,000 to save, fixing at 5 per cent for three years could mean securing around £3,000 in interest, compared with around £2,240 earned based on the current average new savings rate at 3.60 per cent.

open image in gallery ( Getty Images )

“Around £750 extra is not a small amount and teaches a valuable lesson that savers don’t need to have more money to get a better return - instead they may just need to move money they already have. However, fixed bonds are designed for those who are comfortable locking their money away for the full term, so savers should ensure they won’t need to access their cash before committing.”

Ms Eastell also served a reminder that competitive deals “can be short-lived, so those considering a switch would be wise to act sooner rather than later.”

It’s worth noting, of course, you can earn even higher interest, for much smaller monthly amounts, in regular saver accounts.

Which account type and which exact one you pick depends on your needs in terms of timelines, accessing cash, putting more in along the way...and the interest rate. And for most people, there should be room for more than one type of savings account in their wider plan.

The 5 per cent account is very much back, so wherever you choose to park your money, make sure it’s earning great interest well above the rate of inflation.

News.title: Race for vaccine against new Ebola strain gets $8.5m boost
News.content:
The “most promising” vaccine to tackle the Ebola strain behind an explosive outbreak in the Congo has been given an $8.5 million boost, as researchers race to develop an effective shot.

So far at least 3,360 people have been infected and 1,487 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in an epidemic triggered by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola.

But unlike past outbreaks of the more common Zaire strain, there are currently no approved vaccines to tackle Bundibugyo.

On Thursday, the Coalition of Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi) revealed up to $8.5 million of funding for the only single-dose inoculation, which was described as the “most promising vaccine candidate” by the World Health Organization (WHO) in an analysis in May.

It is being developed by researchers at Hilleman Laboratories – a unique partnership between the pharmaceutical giant Merck and the British philanthropic powerhouse Wellcome, which is headquartered in Singapore.

The vaccine candidate is a Bundibugyo version of the Ervebo shot, which was created by Merck (MSD in Europe) and has already been approved for Ebola Zaire.

It uses a rVSV platform, where a modified version of VSV virus is used to train the immune system to react to target pathogens – in this instance, the Bundibugyo species replaces Zaire.

News.title: AMR chatbot could prevent drug-resistant infections in African hospitals
News.content:
A phone-based chatbot advising medics how to prescribe antibiotics has helped raise the quality of care in African hospitals and should stop bugs developing dangerous resistance, developers say.

Staff at four hospitals across Zambia and Kenya have been using two digital tools in a pilot project to try to address one of the world’s biggest health threats.

Anti-microbial resistance (AMR) is caused by germs evolving so that medicines such as antibiotics designed to kill them no longer work.

The menace is linked to nearly five million deaths each year and makes it increasingly difficult to treat infections. The annual death toll could nearly double in the next 25 years, according to some forecasts.

The rise in AMR is being significantly driven by the misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in human medicine and in agriculture.

Using antibiotics when they are not necessary, using the wrong ones, or getting the dosage wrong, all add to the chances that bugs will develop resistance.

With a shortage of new drugs in the development pipeline, one push to defeat AMR has been to get medics to stick to existing prescription, dosage and treatment advice.

The Antibiotic Stewardship Programme through Innovation, Research, and Education (ASPIRE) is trying to give them guidance using technology they already have in their pockets.

News.title: Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC
News.content:
Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at this year’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, following on from her third place at the 2018 Games in Australia.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

News.title: Explosive mpox outbreak causes 3,000 cases in Madagascar
News.content:
More than 3,000 cases of mpox have been recorded in Madagascar after the virus spread from a single port city to some of the country’s busiest coastal hubs.

A total of 3,022 cases and 20 deaths have been recorded as of this week, with cases in Toamasina and Taolagnaro accounting for more than half of all diagnoses.

The outbreak has been linked to Clade 1b mpox, a strain that emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2024, prompting the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare a global public health emergency at the time.

“The main factor driving the continued spread of the disease is human mobility, seeding new outbreaks in areas where the virus has not circulated before,” Professor Carlos Maluquer de Motes of the University of Surrey told The Telegraph.

“Under-reporting is likely, with the real number of cases exceeding what is being reported.”

News.title: Chelsea in 10-goal thriller as ‘Alonso ball’ brings risk and reward
News.content:
Chelsea’s first match under the management of Xabi Alonso was a 10-goal thriller in Australia, as the Premier League side eventually showed their class in a 6-4 win over Western Sydney Wanderers.

Star striker João Pedro, who was controversially left out of Brazil’s World Cup squad, scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming off the bench with half an hour of the friendly remaining.

Alonso had selected a youthful team for the first hour before bringing nine senior players, including João Pedro, into the side in the second half. According to Transfermarkt, Chelsea’s squad is valued at over £1.3bn while their opponents a more modest £5.86m.

Teenage signing Dastan Satpayev, midfielder Dario Essugo and winger Jamie Gittens also found the net for Chelsea, who were defensively vulnerable for long spells for the game.

Here are five things Telegraph Sport learned from Alonso’s first match.

João Pedro picks up where he left off

João Pedro scored 13 goals in the second half of last season and his impressive performances resulted in the 24-year-old being named Chelsea’s player of the campaign. It was something of a surprise, then, when he was left out of Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad this summer.

The good news for Chelsea is that João Pedro’s absence from the World Cup has given him plenty of time to recover ahead of the new campaign, and he looked thrillingly sharp in his second-half performance against Western Sydney Wanderers. The difference in class between João Pedro and Liam Delap, the man he replaced, was clear for all to see.

Two of the Brazilian’s three goals were classy, composed finishes — and he also created a goal for Gittens after surging past three defenders on the left wing. João Pedro looks like he means business.

News.title: China’s chip breakthrough triggers global tech rout
News.content:
China has achieved a breakthrough in developing technology crucial to the AI boom, overcoming US efforts to limit Beijing’s access to the systems.

China’s chip giant Shanghai Yuliangsheng has started production of deep ultraviolet lithography machines, according to The Information, a tech publication.

These machines, which can reach the size of a double-decker bus, use high-powered lasers to imprint designs on to silicon wafers, which are used to make chips.

Until recently, only Western companies and allies of the US had the capability to produce these machines.

The most advanced versions of the technology have largely been the preserve of companies such as Dutch giant ASML and Japan’s Nikon.

These machines have been cut off from China by US export controls, preventing their production of advanced chips as Washington seeks to slow the development of AI in the country.

Semiconductor stocks plunged on the report. Trading was briefly halted on South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index after it suffered a collapse of nearly 11pc overnight, following a bleak day on Wall Street.

Advanced semiconductors, such as those used in AI chips, rely on minuscule circuits, invisible to the naked eye. They can only be manufactured by directing tiny lasers onto microchip wafers, a process known as ultraviolet lithography.

Sports.title: Arsenal star Ethan Nwaneri attracting transfer interest from Dortmund but will get chance to impress Mikel Arteta first
Sports.content:
ARSENAL starlet Ethan Nwaneri is attracting interest from Borussia Dortmund.

The midfielder, 19, faces an uncertain future this summer after spending the second half of last season on loan at Marseille.



Nwaneri made just 11 appearances for the French club and is back with the Gunners now for pre-season.

Arsenal have plenty of playmakers in their squad and that could impact the youngster’s minutes this season.



Eberechi Eze and Martin Odegaard are both options in the No10 role, while 16-year-old Max Dowman is also on the scene.

Borussia Dortmund are aware of the situation and tracking Nwaneri in case the decision is made for him to leave this summer.



That has not been determined yet and the midfielder should get minutes in pre-season to impress Mikel Arteta.

The Gunners have their first friendly on Saturday when they will take on Girona in Spain.

Nwaneri is likely to start the match given Eze and Odegaard are not in training, with fellow midfielders Declan Rice, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino also still on holiday after the World Cup.

Dortmund have a history of developing young English talent and can point to Jude Bellingham’s rise as a prime example.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The German giants, who are also interested in Tottenham wonderkid Mikey Moore, have a long-standing interest in Nwaneri and they were sniffing around him a year ago.

The England Under-21 star ended up signing a new five-year contract and that will expire in the summer of 2030.

Arsenal want to add to their squad this summer after winning the Premier League last season, but are conscious of the need to make sales.

Nwaneri is expected to attract plenty of interest if he is on the market – from both Prem sides and those in Europe.



Another loan move could be an option given he still has plenty of time to run on his contract and is only 19 years old.

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League star sentenced to eight and a half years in jail for sexual assault given permission to join new club
Sports.content:
FOOTIE SHAME Ex-Premier League star sentenced to eight and a half years in jail for sexual assault given permission to join new club

RAFA MIR has been given permission to join a new club despite being sentenced to prison for sexual assault.

Last month he was sentenced to eight and a half years for the rape and assault of a young woman in August 2024.



Mir, 29, has denied in court that the assault took place in his home in Spanish town Bétera and claimed that it was consensual.

He was also slapped with a 13-year restraining order that forbids him from going within 500 metres of his victim and has been ordered to pay more than £55,000 in damages.



He has appealed the verdict, and the prosecutor has said he will not enter prison until the end of the appeal.

Despite this, he was convicted of the crime, which brought his career at Sevilla in LaLiga to an end.

He spent the last two seasons on loan away from the club at Valencia and Elche.

His contract at Sevilla has now been terminated, leaving him on the free agent market.

He is now reportedly set to sign for Greek club Aris Thessaloniki, but there is a condition on him in order to live outside of Spain.

Mir has had to obtain permission from the Provincial Court of Valencia to approve his relocation for work.



He will have to sign in every month at the Spanish consulate in Thessaloniki.

As Greece is a part of the EU, any non-compliance would lead to a European arrest warrant being invoked.

Mir previously spent three seasons contracted to Wolverhampton Wanderers in the Premier League.



He only appeared twice in the league for the club and had a loan spell at then-Championship outfit Nottingham Forest.

The striker played four times for Wolves and 13 times for Forest but never scored a goal for either side.

He has once found the net on English soil, which came for Sevilla in a 3-1 Champions League defeat to Manchester City in 2022.

At Aris, he will now be team-mates with former Manchester City prospect and Watford midfielder Tom Dele Bashiru.

Sports.title: Eddie Howe showed his class in final act as Newcastle manager before walking away over transfer window nightmare
Sports.content:
EDDIE HOWE told Newcastle he wanted to leave two weeks ago – but vowed to stay on until they found his replacement.

The Toon boss has left by mutual consent after the club moved for German Matthias Jaissle from Saudi side Al Alhi.



And Howe only found out this morning that he was allowed to leave after the Magpies agreed a deal with Jaissle.

Howe held talks with Newcastle chiefs at the end of the season where he told them he was happy to continue with the aim of winning the Premier League title by 2030.



But he changed his mind after a frustrating summer in the transfer market which has seen top stars depart.

Anthony Gordon was sold to Barcelona for £70million and Sandro Tonali joined Tottenham in a £100m deal – with captain Bruno Guimaraes expected to follow them out by joining Arsenal.

Howe was told the club wanted to focus on signing younger players – despite missing out on deals for winger Victor Munoz and midfielder Johan Manzambi, who joined Liverpool and Aston Villa respectively.

The Toon boss believed the 2030 title target was unrealistic with the transfer policy but didn’t want to leave them in the lurch.

His exit was finally sealed once they had decided Jaissle – who spent time at the Red Bull clubs famed for signing young stars like Erling Haaland – was the right man to replace him.

Howe, 48, intends to take a break from football although he won’t be short of offers – and he will be a long-term contender to replace Thomas Tuchel as England boss in the future.

EDDIE HOWE'S RECORD AT NEWCASTLE EDDIE HOWE will forever be a Newcastle legend after leading the Toon to their first trophy in 70 years. But that Carabao Cup win, and two Champions League qualifications, weren’t enough to keep everyone happy on Tyneside. Here is Howe’s Newcastle record: Premier League 2021-22 – 11th (19th when he took over) 2022-23 – 4th 2023-24 – 7th 2024-25 – 5th 2025-26 – 12th Trophies won Carabao Cup 2024-25

The 48-year-old joined Newcastle in 2021 and led them to the Champions League and the Carabao Cup last year – their first trophy in 70 years.

Howe has had to work under tight financial rules in the Prem and Europe – despite Newcastle being the richest club in the world.

Last season striker Alexander Isak was sold to Liverpool in a £125m deal, while Elliot Anderson was sold to Nottingham Forest for £35m the year before to help juggle the books.



Anderson, now a starter for England, joined Manchester City for £116m earlier this month.

Toon legend Alan Shearer said: “Thank you to Eddie for what he’s given us.

“He gave me my best day as a Newcastle fan with that day at Wembley.

“He’s given us some incredible nights in the Champions League that we’ll never ever forget.

“It’s been an incredible ride. Whatever happens now, the Geordies will always be grateful for what he gave us that day.



“He won’t be short of offers.”

Sports.title: ‘His place in history books is secured’ – Man Utd announce transfer of boyhood fan Tyler Fredricson
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED academy graduate Tyler Fredricson has left the club – but his name will remain etched in Carrington history.

Fredricson, 21, is joining Swiss top tier side Lausanne-Sport after rising through the ranks at Old Trafford from Under-9s.



He departs with four senior appearances to his name but an impressive junior CV.

Defender Fredricson won the prestigious FA Youth Cup with the Under-18s in 2022.



The squad that beat Nottingham Forest includes goalie Radek Vitek as well as Kobbie Mainoo and Alejandro Garnacho.

Fredricson missed that game through illness but played every minute in the five previous rounds as United scored 15 goals on their way to the showpiece event in front of thousands.

And three years later he made his first-team debut as a starter in a 1-0 loss away at Wolves.

He was in the team two weeks later for a 4-3 defeat at Brentford, achieving a dream of playing for his boyhood side.

Fredricson was named on the bench a handful of other times and is described by United as “a model professional throughout his time with the club and a popular member of our Academy squads.”

The club added: “He worked diligently while proudly rising through the ranks of our world-famous youth system.”

Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED fans are all giddy after watching Matthijs de Ligt step up his recovery.

The Dutch defender, 26, has been out since November with a back injury which sidelined him for most of last season.



Standard rehab did not solve the issue so De Ligt had corrective surgery in May.

The former Ajax, Juventus and Bayern Munich star has not been involved in United’s pre-season tour, and is set to miss the start of the competitive campaign.



But fans may not have much longer to wait before seeing him back in action on the evidence of his latest social media post.

De Ligt was seen moving freely while performing a high knee step-up in the gym, as well as a deadlift with several heavy plates on each side of the bar.



And supporters are starting to realise that, with everyone back fit, the Red Devils could be a formidable side this coming season.

One wrote on X: “We have a scary team if everyone is 100% fit.”

Another put: “De Ligt out here treating pre-season like a war while the rest of the squad are still arguing over who gets the window seat on the plane back.”

A third added: “We have a team that is capable of winning everything, anything.”

And a fourth said: “Him and the butcher could be a top centre-back partnership next season.”

De Ligt, who was limited to just 13 Premier League appearances last term, will want to establish himself as a nailed-on starter under Michael Carrick.



Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Ayden Heaven can also play at centre-back, giving the boss plenty of options to choose from.

While United have strengthened their midfield with the additions of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans for a combined £85million.

Sports.title: Eddie Howe’s exit threatens to put Saudi project back where it began with financially hand-cuffed Toon forced to rebuild
Sports.content:
EDDIE HOWE admitted he had lost control on Wednesday before finally conceding defeat hours later.

And with on-pitch leader, skipper Bruno Guimaraes, also pushing to go, has the world’s richest club lost it too?



For all their wealth, football’s financial rules have proven to be one thing that unlimited wealth from the Middle East has not been able to blow out the water with cheque books.

They also remain powerless to stop the so-called elite from picking off their best players.



Howe’s exit is a pivotal moment on and off the pitch at Newcastle.

And it could have put the whole Saudi Public Investment Fund’s Toon project right back where it began.

For all the celebrations regarding the 2021 takeover, it is now at a major crossroads.

And German Matthias Jaissle faces one heck of a job getting it back on track.

While new stadium plans and a plush new training complex continue to be worked on behind the scenes, financial constraints have the club hand-cuffed on the field.

And with big name after big name scrambling to jump ship, a major reset is occurring.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Jaissle has been tasked with leading the ambitious and youthful new project.

But it will take some job to replicate the success of the man whose boots he is filling.

Howe, who twice got the Mags to the brink of cracking the big time, was fighting a losing battle on Tyneside from the moment Alexander Isak went on strike last year.

It should have been all stations go after securing Newcastle’s first major trophy for 70 years and qualifying for the Champions League for the second time in three years.



But instead the clouds were gathering before the almighty storm of what transpired to be his final year at the helm.

Hopes of building on the Carabao Cup triumph and mounting a title challenge went out the door with Isak’s eventual British record £125m move to Liverpool.

A host of players bought with that cash – in a window Howe was forced to operate without a sporting director – flopped.

And without his Swedish hitman firing them in, Newcastle dropped.



EDDIE HOWE'S RECORD AT NEWCASTLE EDDIE HOWE will forever be a Newcastle legend after leading the Toon to their first trophy in 70 years. But that Carabao Cup win, and two Champions League qualifications, weren’t enough to keep everyone happy on Tyneside. Here is Howe’s Newcastle record: Premier League 2021-22 – 11th (19th when he took over) 2022-23 – 4th 2023-24 – 7th 2024-25 – 5th 2025-26 – 12th Trophies won Carabao Cup 2024-25

Belief that the mega-rich Saudi PIF owners could bankroll a new star-studded team this summer evaporated as the Mags entered a settlement agreement with Uefa for breaching their financial rules.

Last term’s top scorer Anthony Gordon was sold to Barcelona for £75m last month before Italian midfielder Sandro Tonali was flogged to Tottenham in a £100m deal.

Now with Brazilian captain Guimaraes wanting out to Arsenal, the game is finally up for Howe on Tyneside, who realised the departure of a fourth prominent player left him without the ability to meet expectations.

Manchester United are also lurking for Lewis Hall too, the left-back who thrived under mentor Howe and shared an agent with his now old boss.

And from the outside in, a few more could go before next month’s big Premier League kick off.



Discussing Guimaraes after the dismal 4-1 pre-season loss at Bristol City, Howe admitted: “We can’t control the forces that are at play here.”

Hours later he knew it was all over, informing both his staff and the club of his desire to go and take a break from football.

The last six months have been a headache.



Against the backdrop of a depleted squad and performances dropping, the pressure continued to be piled on by PIF and CEO Hopkinson, continuously declaring the target to be challenging the planet’s best within four years.

The Mags missed out on Europe and Howe knew what was coming as the vultures began to circle around his top talents.

He considered his own future too as he got to grips with the club’s new transfer policy of targeting young, unproven talents they could hopefully polish into gems.

He opted to give it a go.

His big guns headed off, four players brought in as replacements were all aged 20 and under, and the realisation eventually dawned on him.



It was time to go.

The baton has now been handed over.

Whether Jaissle, currently managing Saudi Arabian side Al-Ahli (also owned by PIF) but set to replace Howe, can meet Hopkinson’s expectation to be title challengers by 2030 remains to be seen.



Hopkinson is chipping away, bringing in sponsorship deals with Knox, to improve financials.

Meanwhile sporting director Ross Wilson continues to scour the planet for more young, rough stones to hopefully turn into sparkling gems.

But for now, and more importantly for fans that are already fed up of waiting for news on a future stadium, it is on the pitch where it matters.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And it will be down to 38-year-old Jaissle to prove with his assembled squad of kids and old Geordie veterans like Dan Burn that, nearly five years into the grand Saudi experiment, momentum has not truly ground to a dead halt.

Sports.title: ‘Soccer is reflection of life’ – Newcastle target Jaissle has own cheesy website where he gives his football philosophy

SOON to be Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle has his own website – and it’s extremely cheesy.

The German, who has spent the last three years in Saudi Arabia in charge of Al-Ahli, describes himself as being “emotional on the sidelines.”

After retiring early due to injury – Jaissle hung up his boots in 2014 at Hoffenheim having moved there for free from Stuttgart, where he went through the academy – he has been in coaching ever since.



A product of the Red Bull multi-club system, he spent time as assistant in RB Leipzig‘s youth setup before heading to Brondby in Denmark.

His first managerial role was at AKA Salzburg Under-18 and then into the senior game at FC Liefering, also in Austria.



From there he progressed to the adult side at Salzburg, staying for two years and winning the domestic title twice as well as the cup.

Sports.title: Incoming Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle is disciple of ex-Man Utd boss known for stylish football and dress sense
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE have turned to a disciple of Ralf Rangnick as they look to replace Eddie Howe.

Matthias Jaissle, 38, is expected to jump into the hot seat at St. James’ Park after the bombshell news of Howe’s departure.



Becoming the Magpies head coach would cap off a remarkable rise for Jaissle, who currently manages Saudi Arabian side Al Ahli.

The German was a talented centre-back, but was forced to retire in 2014 at the age of just 26 after never truly recovering from a knee injury picked up five years earlier.



Former Manchester United boss Rangnick came to Jaissle’s aid after that and invited him on a trainee programme with RB Leipzig’s youth academy.

The pair knew each other as Rangnick coached a young Jaissle during his time as manager of Hoffenheim and he reached out in his new role as RB Leipzig’s head of sport.



Jaissle rose through the ranks in the Red Bull network and eventually landed the job as head coach of RB Salzburg in 2021 at the age of 33.

The German won the Austrian Bundesliga in both his two seasons in charge and was heralded as one of the brightest young coaches in Europe.

That is a point made on the coach’s own personal website – https://matthias-jaissle.com/ – that charts his rise.

The opening line on the site reads: “Football is a reflection of life. Victories. Defeats. Joy. Sorrow. Passion. It’s all part of it.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“Matthias Jaissle experienced it himself. As a player whose career had to end far too early due to injury. And as a coach who celebrated several titles at a young age.”

Those titles have continued in Saudi Arabia, where Jaissle has been managing Al Ahli since 2023.

He has won the Asian Champions League Elite twice and the Saudi Super Cup in his time out there.



Jaissle can argue he has done it in style, too. Not only with his football on the pitch, but also his clothes off it.

He is renowned for being a snappy dresser and early in his career that led to comparisons with Julian Nagelsmann.

It was not a hard parallel to draw, given Jaissle was a young and trendy German coach who liked to play attacking football.



But, in 2022, he said: “I’m not Julian Nagelsmann 2.0. I’m Matthias Jaissle.”

Jaissle insists he has his own style, but having honed his skill in the Red Bull model there is an obvious influence from Rangnick.

The German told GiveMeSport in 2024: “I have always tried to be authentic as a coach and find my own way.



“Of course, I have influences. Ralf Rangnick played a big part in developing my ideas because I played under him for most of my playing career.

“And in my youth, I had Thomas Tuchel, so I have followed his principles and career. Then there’s Jurgen Klopp – I often looked at the transitions he put in place with Liverpool.

“In possession, I like how Pep Guardiola finds structure and balance. And there’s a lot to take from Roberto De Zerbi’s build-up as well. It’s a constant learning process.

“I am always refining my style, but essentially, and I know it’s easy to say, we want dominance in all phases of the game.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It’s a never-ending process because you always need to develop your ideas as a coach without abandoning your roots.



“At Salzburg, I played a 4-4-2 with a diamond midfield. At Al-Ahli, we use a 4-2-3-1 system. You have to adjust to the squad you have as well as the circumstances.”

The Red Devils have continued their push to sign more midfield talent this summer, adding Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos whilst at least one more could also arrive. Reinforcements in attack and at left-back are also on their radar.

All have had loan spells away and both temporary and permanent exits are on the cards, reports the Daily Mail. Goalkeeper Vitek impressed at Bristol City last season and enquiries have been made for him. Harry Amass, who was at Norwich previously, is also of interest.

Sports.title: England told they must BOYCOTT 2030 World Cup in response to Gianni Infantino plan
Sports.content:
England told they must BOYCOTT 2030 World Cup in response to Gianni Infantino plan

England have been told to consider boycotting the next World Cup by several former FA bosses as organisations unite to reject FIFA's proposal, which is led by Gianni Infantino

View 2 Images A boycott of the World Cup by leading nations would put a spanner in FIFA's plans (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

Several former FA chiefs have urged England to snub the next World Cup in response to Gianni Infantino's plan to sell stakes in FIFA's major tournaments.

‌



The FIFA president has announced his proposal, which has been widely condemned across the footballing world, as he seeks to create a commercial subsidiary to run its main events - and outside investors will be able to purchase those stakes.

‌



UEFA have called out FIFA and that has led to backlash from federations in Asia and North America. The FA have said they were "completely unaware of this proposal" and they are "deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance".

‌



Several men who have stood at the top of English football have taken aim at FIFA's plans and have backed extreme measures in a bid to rebel against FIFA - which includes not playing at the next World Cup that is being held in Spain and Portugal.

19 countries have pulled out of World Cup as UEFA threaten Gianni Infantino boycott READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino responds to furious backlash over World Cup sale as nations consider boycott READ MORE :

David Bernstein, who took a public stand against Infantino’s predecessor Sepp Blatter when he was FA chairman, claimed that the FIFA plan “stinks” and England should "have to have the guts” to boycott the World Cup.

Mark Palios, the former FA chief executive, said: “UEFA have a real card to play, and that is if they don’t turn up at the next World Cup that’s going to be an absolute financial disaster for FIFA.”

‌



He added: “If you don’t have Spain, France, England, Germany there, then it’s not going to be anything like the spectacle that it normally is. That’s the major card they have to play and I hope they do play that.”

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's World Cup plan is seen as a money grab (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

The divide between UEFA and FIFA is already well established with Aleksander Ceferin and Infantino not seeing eye-to-eye, so much so that Ceferin didn't attend the World Cup. Europe's governing body were outspoken about some of the decisions taken in the World Cup, including the Folarin Balogun red card saga.

‌



Infantino has attempted to sell his plan and claimed on Wednesday: "It is an opportunity but not an obligation. It is a golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally. But again, it is just an offer, not an obligation."

The FIFA boss also tried to sweeten supporters by suggesting: "Fans from everywhere in the world would gain immeasurably from this game-changing potential because it will transform football in their countries."

Sports.title: Alan Shearer shares honest take on Eddie Howe’s Newcastle exit and selling best players
Sports.content:
Alan Shearer shares honest take on Eddie Howe’s Newcastle exit and selling best players

Eddie Howe is expected to leave his role as Newcastle United boss after five years in charge at St James' Park

View 2 Images Alan Shearer has given his verdict on Eddie Howe's impending departure from Newcastle (Image: Michael Driver | MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Alan Shearer has expressed his true gratitude to Eddie Howe for the work he's done at his beloved Newcastle United after news emerged of his impending departure.

‌



It suddenly emerged on Thursday morning that Howe would be leaving his role as Magpies boss, which sees his five-year spell at St James’ Park come to an end.

‌



Wednesday night saw Newcastle suffer a 4-1 defeat to Bristol City in their second pre-season friendly of the summer, in what will be Howe’s final match in charge of the club.

‌



As reported by Chronicle Live, Howe informed his backroom staff of his decision to leave Newcastle after the squad returned to Tyneside from their Bristol flight, and the 48-year-old’s replacement is set to be Matthias Jaissle.

Howe is expected to depart having claimed one major honour during his tenure at St James' Park, with the Magpies lifting the Carabao Cup in the 2024/25 season.

Eddie Howe told what made his Newcastle job 'unsustainable' before sudden departure READ MORE :

Eddie Howe's final words as Newcastle boss speak volumes after Toon exit READ MORE :

Newcastle sealed a 2-1 victory over Liverpool at Wembley Stadium, bringing an end to the club's 70-year wait for a major piece of silverware.

‌



Shearer took to social media to post a photograph of Howe holding the Carabao Cup following their triumph over Liverpool at Wembley in 2025, accompanied by a heartfelt message to the departing boss.

"Thanks Eddie. You gave us this day," Shearer wrote in his social media post.

The Newcastle legend went on to voice his surprise at Howe's forthcoming departure, adding a further message to the outgoing manager.

‌



"I’m very, very surprised with the news that Eddie Howe is leaving Newcastle," Shearer told Betfair. "I guess it's strange timing with three weeks to go until the new season kicks off.

"I don't know what's gone on, whether it was the end of last season, whether it was the summer, whether he feels they can't continue to sell his best players. I’m led to believe it was Eddie’s decision to leave."

He added: "What I would say is thank you. Thank you to Eddie for what he's given us. I mean, he gave me my best day as a Newcastle fan with that day at Wembley. He's given us some incredible nights in the Champions League that we'll never ever forget.

‌



"He did a wonderful job for Newcastle, so it’s a huge thank you to Eddie.

View 2 Images Eddie Howe is expected to leave Newcastle United (Image: Ian MacNicol, Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"It's been an incredible ride. I think the job that he did was unbelievable from where he took us when he came, there was a real threat of relegation. He steadied the ship.

"He then got us climbing the league. He then brought in some wonderful players. He then took us to a final; we got beaten in that final, but then took us back again and gave us the day that we've so craved for.

"I've been to Wembley as a player and lost. I've been to Wembley as a fan and lost. But I've also had the pleasure of going to Wembley and winning thanks to Eddie. Whatever happens now, the Geordies will always be grateful for what he gave us that day."

‌



The announcement of Howe's departure follows the club's first two pre-season friendlies of the summer, with the Magpies also being held to a 1-1 draw against Gateshead last week.

Uncertainty also continues to surround the future of Bruno Guimaraes, who is being heavily linked with a switch to Arsenal this summer.

Newcastle have already lost Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali this summer, while Alexander Isak also left the club nearly 12 months ago.

‌



Howe was quizzed about Guimaraes' prospects at Newcastle less than 24 hours before news broke of his own imminent exit.

"What will be, will be,” Howe said after the defeat to Bristol City. “We can’t control the forces that are at play here, we’ve just got to make sure that when Bruno comes back, we look after him and he trains well, which I’m sure he will do.

"And he makes a difference as he always has done."

Sports.title: Eddie Howe was FAILED by Newcastle United owners - he should have walked away earlier
Sports.content:
In late March, David Hopkinson, chief executive of Newcastle United, was asked about Eddie Howe’s future. And this is how he replied: “I don’t have a stance on his future. I expect to have a great run to the end of the season and we’ll talk about the future when it is time.”

It is a wonder Howe did not walk out of St James’ Park there and then.

What Hopkinson should have said is that the club has a manager who has taken them from the lower reaches of the Premier League to TWO Champions League campaigns and has helped them to a first domestic trophy in 70 years.

He should have said Howe, over a period of four and a half years, has brilliantly managed a club that is notoriously difficult to manage, and that they would be doing all they can to make sure he was happy to lead them for many seasons to come.

‌



Instead, he did not ‘have a stance on his future’.

Eddie Howe's final words as Newcastle boss speak volumes after Toon exit READ MORE :

Howe had given life and soul to re-energising a great institution and that was his thanks. That was an ill-advised interview from Hopkinson.

The chief executive might claim to have just chosen the wrong words. But more significantly, Howe was let down by actions, as well as words.

The club had little choice but to take Liverpool’s £125million for Alexander Isak and in Anthony Gordon’s case, it is hard to stop a player going to Barcelona. You can even make a compelling argument that £100million for Sandro Tonali was too good an offer to turn down, although losing one of his best players to Tottenham, who had just finished 17th, must have been a very bitter pill for Howe to swallow.

‌



But by the looks of it, they are about to sell Bruno Guimaraes, their talisman. That was probably the final straw for Howe, who has seen the Saudi owners promise the moon, but, since Howe's magic produced a trophy, delivered very little against what they promised

The executives and owners will argue that it is hard to keep players who want to leave and that they have to trade - buy AND sell - to comply with the Premier League’s financial regulations. Fair enough.

But it is the job of the executives and the owners to make sure the marquee players do not want to leave. When they want to leave in numbers, the executives and owners are not doing something right.

‌



Which is why, in a way, Howe’s tenure might have come to a natural end, and the suggestions are that his departure has been amicable. He is such a respectful character that Howe - who is likely to be succeeded by Al-Ahli’s 38-year-old German manager, Matthias Jaissle - is not likely to say anything different when he does talk about leaving a job he clearly loved for a long time.

View 2 Images Eddie Howe and Bruno Guimaraes (Image: Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

It's understood Howe had wanted to leave for two weeks, with an exit plan in place since early in pre-season.

Neither Newcastle CEO David Hopkinson and sporting director Ross Wilson were shocked by his departure today. Howe's exit is deemed an "energy thing", and club sources insist that it is NOT about politics or transfers or the players that have been signed in the last month or so.

‌



But Howe's comments at Ashton Gate, after being trounced 4-1 by Bristol City in a pre-season friendly on Wednesday night, particularly on Guimaraes - declaring wistfully "what will be, will be" - suggested different.

Some fans might point to a turbulent season that saw Newcastle finish 12th in the Premier League as evidence that his time on Tyneside was coming to an end. No matter that they made it to the last 16 of the Champions League and to the Carabao Cup semi-finals.

When you look beyond the fact that Jaissle is coming from the Saudi Pro League, it will be an intriguing appointment if it happens.

But you can’t help feeling Howe could have created a dynasty in Newcastle and that it is a shame it is over.

‌

Sports.title: Eddie Howe told what made his Newcastle job 'unsustainable' before sudden departure
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe told what made his Newcastle job 'unsustainable' before sudden departure

Eddie Howe has left Newcastle United after a five-year tenure in surprising fashion, but one former Premier League star saw the writing on the wall after last season's tough watch at St James' Park

View 2 Images Eddie Howe has left Newcastle United (Image: David Davies/PA Wire)

Dwight Yorke believes that Newcastle United's home and away losses to Sunderland AFC last season made Eddie Howe's job 'unsustainable.' He also believes that finishing five places below them in the Premier League didn't help matters.

‌



The 48-year-old has decided to part ways with the Magpies after a largely successful five-year tenure, with Matthias Jaissle touted to take the reins at St James' Park following his exit. It comes after months of criticism from select Newcastle fans, coupled with the club's damning approach to the summer transfer window thus far.

‌



The Magpies have already lost Anthony Gordon to Barcelona and Sandro Tonali to Tottenham Hotspur, and are on the verge of parting ways with club captain, Bruno Guimaraes, amid a wealth of interest from Arsenal. That would ultimately leave Howe without star talent for the upcoming season, making it incredibly difficult to improve on last term's 12th-place finish.

‌



However, the performances on the pitch in 2025/26, particularly against their biggest rivals, were especially problematic for Howe, with Yorke claiming that back-to-back losses to the Black Cats made the Englishman's position 'unsustainable.'

Speaking to BOYLE Sports, who offer football odds, Yorke - who played for Sunderland between 2006 and 2009 - said: "Eddie Howe losing twice to Sunderland and finishing below them last season didn’t resonate very well with the fans.

Eddie Howe to leave Newcastle with immediate effect as replacement lined up READ MORE :

Premier League rival and six other clubs Eddie Howe could join after shock Newcastle United exit READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"It doesn’t matter where you are in the world, when it comes to your local derby, you cannot lose both of those games in a season. No matter what else is going on against the other teams, you have to get a result in these games.

"To lose both home and away to your rival like that, it’s unsustainable because the local fans know what comes with it."

It was an increasingly tough watch for Newcastle United fans last season, who lost local bragging rights with an inability to defeat Regis Le Bris' Sunderland. The Black Cats hosted the Magpies at the Stadium of Light in December, winning 1-0 through a catastrophic Nick Woltemade own-goal.

‌



View 2 Images Eddie Howe during Newcastle United's defeat to Sunderland at St. James' Park (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

While Newcastle were heavy favourites to atone for the loss during March's reverse at St James' Park, Sunderland prospered once again. While Gordon opened the scoring for his team just 10 minutes into play, Chemsdine Talbi levelled matters early in the second-half.

Brian Brobbey then converted from close range at the death to secure a 2-1 win for Sunderland, and bragging rights for another season. It comes as Al-Ahly coach Jaissle is set to take up tenure on Tyneside following Howe's departure.

Sports.title: Reinvigorate Root and fix culture: What's in new Test coach Fleming's in-tray?
Sports.content:
England have announced the appointment of Stephen Fleming as coach of the men's Test team and he will take over after the three-Test series against Pakistan. We take a look at the jobs on his to-do list ahead of a bumper year…

Reinvigorate Root

Ben Stokes' shock - and extravagant, considering it came at 3.25pm while he was midway through a bowling spell - retirement from international cricket meant England needed a captain to lead them post-Bazball.

Enter Joe Root. The former skipper - who has captained the most all-time England Tests with 65 - is set to take the mantle for a second time after a first five-year stint as captain between 2017 and 2022.

Fleming talked of "bedding in the gains" made by Stokes and Brendon McCullum in his upcoming tenure, and clearly he and the ECB have decided that tried-and-trusted Root - rather than white-ball captain and Test vice-captain Harry Brook - is the man to do just that.

Image: Joe Root has been reappointed as captain, having done it in 65 Tests previously

Root's captaincy, though, is not without its drawbacks. He gave it up after five years in charge having won one Test in his last 17, and told Sky Sports in 2022 that the role had started to have "an unhealthy effect on the rest of my life".

His recent outing as interim Test captain in the absence of Stokes did not do much to reassure doubters. England were subjected to a drubbing, losing the second Test against New Zealand by 253 runs at The Oval in uninspiring fashion.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mark Butcher questioned the decision to name Root as captain

"Joe was completely wrung out at the end of his time as captain for five years," former England batter Mark Butcher told Sky Sports News. "The best thing that happened to him and his game was not being captain any more.

"I think it's a retrograde step for the team... I just don't think it's the best move for him to be captain at this time or at any other moment in time actually."

Fleming's first task, then, has to be readying his veteran leader for the daunting task of a winter tour of South Africa and then the home Ashes next summer.

Develop unfinished-product Brook

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the fifth T20 international between England and India in Southampton as the hosts romped to a 4-0 series win

The new coach and the powers that be have clearly decided Brook is not ready for such a consuming role. He was overlooked as stand-in leader for the Oval Test against New Zealand after the Stokes nightclub saga, having become embroiled in a nightclub drama of his own in New Zealand before an ODI last winter.

Brook, though, reignited conversations after guiding England to a 4-0 T20 series win over India that moved them top of the T20I rankings and a 2-1 ODI series victory over the same opponents. He appears to have a pretty sharp cricketing mind a lot of the time - but, according to Fleming, he needs more time before taking on the red-ball captaincy.

"I'm also excited to work with Harry Brook," Fleming said. "The best players are never finished products, and helping Harry continue to develop his extraordinary talent and his leadership will be an important part of this journey."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights as Root's 99 not out guided England to a four-wicket win over India in the second ODI

Root's reinstatement has ended concerns over whether Brook could captain in all three forms amid such a packed fixture schedule, and will give the white-ball captain more time to develop his leadership and focus on the upcoming 50-over World Cup in 2027.

Root, though, turns 36 in December, and his appointment will most likely solely focus on the bumper year of Test cricket ahead - as it feels difficult to imagine the skipper leading the team much beyond that.

With Brook seemingly the captain-in-waiting, it is perhaps just as incumbent on Fleming to help bring on future leaders as to support the one he has put in place now.

Work with white-ball coach McCullum

Image: Brendon McCullum has been succeeded by Fleming as England Test coach

While splitting the roles between red and white-ball cricket will allow complete focus on one format for each coach - and therefore reduce the risk of burnout - England's two head honchos will need a strong relationship for it to work.

Fleming and McCullum certainly have that. The two played alongside each other for six years for New Zealand - with McCullum making his Test debut under Fleming's captaincy - and they were even investors in a business together, cricHQ.

McCullum has said that "robust" conversations will take place with the Test coach in order to "achieve harmony and success" for English cricket, which can probably be read along the lines of: "I won't be asset stripped."

That harmony feels significantly easier to maintain with two coaches so familiar with each other already.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McCullum speaks on what it will be like working with a new Test coach for England as well as the future of the white-ball side

Test cricket, with that home Ashes in a year's time, is clearly the priority, hence why McCullum was relieved of his red-ball duties following the malaise he oversaw.

But Fleming will not want that to damage England's excellent T20 form or the objective of fixing an ODI side languishing eighth in the rankings and winning the 2027 50-over World Cup.

England fans crave success on all fronts - there has been no global white-ball trophy since 2022, no Ashes win since 2015 - and the coaches must align to make that possible.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following England's Test series defeat to New Zealand, Nasser Hussain gave a scathing review of McCullum's Test-series record

Fix the boozing and off-field indiscipline

England have had more drink-related incidents than their Test side has had wins of late, with Brook's scrap with a bouncer in New Zealand, Ben Duckett seemingly intoxicated during a pilloried beach break in Noosa between Ashes Tests, and then Stokes and Gus Atkinson's curfew-breaking, headline-making trip to a Chelsea nightspot.

How clear the curfew was remains, well, unclear and that is another black mark that can be labelled against this team: lack of attention to detail.

We saw that in their Ashes preparation, with just one warm-up game prior to the Perth Test - and not a particularly useful one at that, in that it was played on a docile surface at Lilac Hill that in no way matched the bouncy deck they would come up against at Optus Stadium. And we all know what happened there…

Image: Ben Stokes is now concentrating on playing for Durham

Batters out driving on the up ad nauseum as England threw away a golden position. Now-interim coach Marcus Trescothick would later say there were no discussions about playing those shots on that surface. Really?!

"There's been a number of times now that we've let ourselves down" incoming captain Root said after England's latest escapade.

"We have to learn from those mistakes and understand that we shouldn't be putting ourselves in those situations."

The ECB issued new additional player behaviour guidelines in July ahead of the three-Test series against Pakistan - it is now up to Fleming and Root to make sure they are followed far better than under Stokes and McCullum.

Replace Stokes and nail down best XI

Image: Rehan Ahmed is an option as England's Test all-rounder

Stokes' departure - unless he can be lured back - not only deprives England of a talismanic captain but also a gun all-rounder, even if his batting form tapered off at the back end of his Test career with just one hundred since the 2023 Ashes.

There is no easy fix here, although Sam Curran is a seam-bowling all-rounder option - his left-arm angle may be useful - while Rehan Ahmed offers a spin-bowling one. Leg-spinner Ahmed's inclusion at No 7 could allow England to play four frontline quicks.

Most of the batting spots look locked in: Bethell at No 3, Root at No 4, Brook at No 5 and possibly, after a timely ton versus New Zealand, Duckett as one opener. Duckett's top-order accomplice is maybe not so certain with Emilio Gay hitting two fifties against the Kiwis but tailing off thereafter. Other county openers will feel they have a chance.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stokes took a wicket moments after announcing his retirement from international cricket

The same will apply for spinners with the two men who made Shoaib Bashir their pet project, Stokes and McCullum, no longer around. Bashir has potential, no doubt, but the new Test coach may want someone with more tangible stats behind them. Jack Leach, perhaps?

Jamie Smith could also be sweating on his spot as wicketkeeper-batter. After a lean Ashes, he did not fare outstandingly against New Zealand, albeit his replacement at The Oval while he was on paternity leave, James Rew, toiled with bat and gloves during a sobering debut.

Win matches and big series

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McCullum reveals what his ambitions were with Bazball after becoming Test coach in 2022

Of all the objectives on the coach's to-do list, this is right at the top of it.

The end of the Bazball era saw just three wins from the final 12 matches, while the whole of the Bazball era saw no series victories over Australia and India - the contests on which England are judged - with 2-2 draws at home to those sides and 4-1 batterings away.

Fleming should not - and most likely will not - abandon every Bazball principle. Attacking, in-your-face cricket got England into a number of match-winning positions over the last four years - only for the players to get too amped up and then chuck those positions away by not reining themselves in. See Lord's 2023, Rajkot 2024 and Perth 2025 as prime examples.

The task is to cut out the brainless bits and make sure refinement and responsibility come when games are in the palm of England's hands, as while English fans obviously enjoy entertaining cricket, they love winning cricket even more.

And they love winning against Australia more than anything. That opportunity arises again next summer, which makes Fleming's appointment crucial.

Sports.title: Chelsea sign Lacroix from Palace
Sports.content:
Chelsea have completed the signing of Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace in a deal worth £51m.

The 26-year-old central defender has signed a six-year contract at Stamford Bridge. Lacroix's arrival takes the club's spending to beyond £250m this summer.

Lacroix becomes the first player Chelsea have signed for a fee aged 26 or over since the summer of 2022, with the club also set to complete deals for 35-year-old Danny Welbeck and 36-year-old Jordan Henderson.

This is a deliberate change in transfer policy from Chelsea to target more experienced palyers that has been embraced by new manager Xabi Alonso.

Palace were seeking around £55m in negotiations, given the fee Tottenham paid for Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton.

Chelsea are expected to move on a number of defenders in this window, including Trevoh Chalobah, Benoit Badiashile and Axel Disasi, having already raised more than £130m from player sales and the compensation received from Manchester City for Enzo Maresca.

Sky Sports News understands Chelsea gave Palace the chance to discuss signing one of their defenders available for transfer during talks.

Palace and Chelsea have a good relationship and they have done deals for players such as Chalobah and Ben Chilwell in the past.

'Chelsea is the best club in the world'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lacroix gives his first interview as a Chelsea player where he speaks on his move to west London. Credit: Chelsea FC

Lacroix said: "I think it's the best move for me because it's the best club in the world.

"I spoke with Malo [Gusto]. I spoke with Trev [Chalobah]. I spoke with Benoit [Badiashile]. It's easy for people to speak well about this club because it has a lot of big history and I'm really proud to be a part of it now.

"I spoke with the manager on the phone. We spoke about tactics, we spoke about how he sees the game. First of all, I was happy just to speak about football with him, and I saw that we have the same direction and desire for this club.

Image: Lacroix is all smiles as he displays his new team's shirt

"When I spoke with the gaffer, when I spoke also with the people I know from the national team who play for Chelsea, like Malo, they told me it was the best club I can go to.

"So already I was saying: "Okay, I don't need to think too much". After talking to people I said to myself: "This is the best step forward for me"."

Sky Sports' Adam Bate:

Far from a veteran, Lacroix, 26, is entering his prime after two strong seasons with Palace. Beyond Selhurst Park, perhaps the Frenchman has gone a little under the radar. But, particularly since Marc Guehi's exit, there is growing awareness of his key role.

Oliver Glasner, who worked with him in both Germany and England, rather summed it up with his own verdict on the player recently. "There is Maxence Lacroix, who came from Wolfsburg, and many asked, 'Why did you sign this player?' I think he stepped up."

Few defenders boast his skillset. Lacroix ranks among the top five fastest centre-backs in the Premier League since his arrival from Wolfsburg in 2024. That recovery speed helps make him one of the most formidable one-on-one defenders in the competition.

The numbers back that up to. In one-on-one situations, nobody is better than Lacroix at winning the ball back. He is the only player in the Premier League to have faced 50 or more such situations in the past two seasons and won the ball more often than not.

At 6ft 4in, Lacroix is a robust physical presence who has adapted easily to the demands of the Premier League. He has all the stats to support that, ranking third for clearances and seventh for aerial duels won. But he can do more than defend his box.

Sports.title: Who is Matthias Jaissle?
Sports.content:
Matthias Jaissle, the man tipped to replace Eddie Howe at Newcastle United, might not be too well known given that his only head coaching roles to date have been in Austria and Saudi Arabia. So who is the man linked with a move to St James' Park?

The 38-year-old German played for Hoffenheim before embarking on a coaching career that took him to Denmark and into an academy role at Red Bull Salzburg. His first senior job was at FC Liefering, moving on to the top job at Salzburg in the summer of 2021.

Jaissle won the double in his first season and retained the league in his second. He worked with Karim Adeyemi and Benjamin Sesko in Salzburg, competing in the Champions League, before moving on to Al Ahli in the Saudi Pro League in 2023.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Eddie Howe’s final interview as Newcastle head coach

He has spent the past three years in the Gulf, winning the Saudi Super Cup in Hong Kong last year. But before that he spoke to Sky Sports as part of our Future of Football series for an illuminating discussion of his ideas and how he saw the game progressing.

Here's what we found out…

Inspirations as a coach

Jaissle is steeped in the Red Bull school, having been the head coach at FC Liefering and Red Bull Salzburg at a young age. This means a particular emphasis on high pressing and relatively direct play, looking to move the ball forwards whenever possible.

But his Salzburg team also had plenty of possession and Jaissle would not want to be pigeonholed. "You have to develop your game, you have to always make progress." He has indicated that he is willing to look to all of the game's top coaches for inspiration.

"They always have some principles you can see which make sense to include in your philosophy. It's not about copying, exactly, but seeing interesting things, creating your thoughts about it, and then, if it fits, you can bring it into your way of playing."

What formation does he play?

That has been reflected in the evolution of his preferred formation. At Salzburg, it was often built around the narrow 4-4-2 with wingers coming inside that Ralf Rangnick popularised across the Red Bull teams. But he switched things up in Saudi Arabia.

With Al Ahli, he often adopted a 4-2-3-1 formation building with either a 3-2-5 or a 2-3-5 structure - something that is de rigueur in the Premier League. Speaking to Sky Sports, he explained that it was more about principles of play than the precise formations.

Image: Red Bull Salzburg's formation in the Champions League under Jaissle

"It is not about formations that much. It is more how you want to play, how you want to attack, how you want to defend. If you understand that and the players understand that, tactically you are much more flexible and the formation is not that important."

It can be demanding for players. "These days the players are more and more involved in tactical things. Every coach and every club works with principles, so every player has to know a lot of things, tactically, in each phase of the game. I think that's a big change."

Predicting the future

Speaking to Sky Sports in 2023, Jaissle anticipated some of the changes that have been seen in the Premier League since then with its increased robustness and the growing focus on set-pieces. "It could be more dynamic and more physical also," he suggested.

He added: "Only the most professional players will survive at the top, top level, I would say." Jaissle also predicted that "there will be more and more so-called all-rounders" in football in the future - meaning defenders who attack, attackers who defend, and more.

"Players who are able to play in more positions, which makes total sense and makes it easier for the manager to change within the game or alter the formation. That is quite easy if the players understand it and know how to live your principles on the pitch."

That extends to the goalkeeper role with his preference for those who can be part of the build-up. "Goalkeeper is not a position by itself any more. It is completely included with the other guys. A goalkeeper has to have an understanding of all phases of the game."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the friendly between Bristol City and Newcastle [Credit: Robins TV]

But motivation still matters

Jaissle has experience working in multi-cultural dressing rooms, citing the fact that the number of different nationalities at Salzburg was into double figures. And for all the focus on tactics, technique and physicality, motivation remains key to management.

"I think the communication and the connection with the players is always the base for leadership and being a good coach," he explained to Sky Sports. "You really have to take care of that. I would always prioritise one on ones and face-to-face conversation.

"You really have to take care that you don't have too much information. This is a big challenge. As a manager or coach, you know so much about tactics, but you cannot just give everything to the players. You have to really take care not to overwhelm them."

Sports.title: Women's Super League fixtures announced for 2026/27 season
Sports.content:
Manchester City will begin their Women's Super League title defence against newly-promoted Birmingham City after London City Lionesses have opened the 2026/27 season against Manchester United, live on Sky Sports.

The fixtures for the upcoming campaign have been released, with kick-off times and broadcast picks confirmed for the first four weekends, featuring more matches than ever after the league expanded from 12 teams to 14 after Birmingham City, Crystal Palace and Charlton Athletic secured promotion from WSL 2.

Sky Sports will show 90 per cent of all WSL matches live on Sky Sports and NOW - 163 matches in total, as well as the play-off - with selected games also shown on the Sky Sports WSL YouTube channel. There will be greater flexibility over fixtures, with fewer matches kicking off at the same time.

London City, who signed two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas this summer, will launch the new season in front of the Sky Sports cameras on Friday September 4 against Man Utd before champions Man City host newcomers Birmingham City on a bumper day of action on Sunday September 6 featuring five live games.

The other matches on the first Sunday of the season see last year's runners-up Arsenal start with a trip to Brighton, while Tottenham host a London derby against West Ham, Liverpool visit newly-promoted Charlton and Crystal Palace, who secured an immediate return to the top flight, face Everton.
