Sports.title: Howe leaves Newcastle - Saudi-based Jaissle set to replace him
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe has left his role as Newcastle United head coach.

The decision has been taken following discussions with the club's hierarchy over the last 48 hours, although Howe had started the ball rolling on a potential departure a number of weeks ago.

In this time, Howe continued to focus on preparing the Newcastle team for their season opener against Liverpool on August 23, live on Sky Sports. Howe's departure comes 25 days before that fixture.

Matthias Jaissle of Al Ahli Is the favourite to replace Howe and Newcastle are hopeful of putting him in charge within 24 hours. Sky Sports News understands talks are at an advanced stage with the 38-year-old German coach. Al Ahli are one of the four clubs owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) - who also own Newcastle.

Kieran McKenna and Antonio Conte were other names on the shortlist before Newcastle decided on Jaissle, who will take charge of Newcastle's pre-season training camp in La Manga.

Newcastle have already had a challenging summer after the sales of Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon - and that continues with uncertainty over their captain Bruno Guimaraes, who is wanted by Arsenal.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Howe discussed the rumours surrounding Bruno Guimaraes and revealed he wanted to keep him at the club, before news of his departure emerged

Those sales have played a factor in Howe's decision amid concerns about what the squad will look like at the start of the new campaign. Newcastle also sold striker Alexander Isak for a British-record £125m to Liverpool last summer.

Howe has spent a number of months reflecting on his time at Newcastle and believed he could take the club forward this season, providing Newcastle recruited well this summer.

Eddie Howe's Newcastle reign November 2021 - Howe replaces Steve Bruce as Newcastle United head coach

May 2022 - Howe guides Newcastle to 11th-placed finish in first season in charge. Newcastle become first Premier League team to stay up after failing to win any of their first 14 games

August 2022 - Howe signs new long-term contract

February 2023 - Howe leads Newcastle to first final in 24 years but they lose Carabao Cup final 2-0 to Manchester United

May 2023 - Howe leads Newcastle to a fourth-placed finish earning the club qualification for the Champions League for the first time in more than 20 years

January 2024 - Howe leads Newcastle to victory in an FA Cup Tyne-Wear derby - their first win over Sunderland in almost 13 years

May 2024 - Newcastle finish seventh despite scoring 85 goals and posting their highest Premier League goal tally ever

Mar 2025 - Newcastle beat Liverpool 2-1 in the Carabao Cup final to win their first major trophy in 56 years

May 2025 - Howe leads Newcastle into the Champions League again with a fifth-placed Premier League finish

September 2025 - Howe loses star striker Alexander Isak to Liverpool in a £125m deal on Deadline Day

February 2026 - Newcastle advance to the knockout stages of the Champions League via the play-offs, where they are later beaten by Barcelona

May 2026 - Newcastle finish the season 12th

May 2026 - Anthony Gordon leaves for Barcelona in a deal that nets Newcastle almost £70m

July 2026 - Howe sees Sandro Tonali leave for Spurs in a deal worth £100m

July 2026 - Club captain Bruno Guimaraes tells Newcastle he wants to leave

July 2026 - Howe steps down as Newcastle head coach less than 24 hours after 4-1 pre-season defeat to Championship side Bristol City

Newcastle have signed 20-year-old winger Bazoumana Toure from Hoffenheim for £42m, 18-year-old midfielder Sean Steur from Ajax for £23m and 20-year-old goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen from Reims for £18.5m.

They have recently, however, appeared to miss out on Johan Manzambi, who decided to move to Aston Villa - which was a big blow for Howe and the club.

Howe has been one of Newcastle's greatest-ever managers, winning the League Cup to end the club's 70-year wait for silverware as well as taking the club into the Champions League on two occasions after sealing top-five finishes in the Premier League.

Last season, they progressed further in the Champions League than they had ever done before.

Howe's final game in charge was a brutal 4-1 pre-season loss to Championship side Bristol City on Wednesday night.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch highlights of the pre-season friendly between Bristol City and Newcastle. Credit: Robins TV

When did Howe decide to leave Newcastle?

Sky Sports News' Keith Downie:

Eddie Howe informed his coaching staff upon return from Bristol City, where they lost 4-1 in a friendly. The decision had nothing to do with the match, it had been in the pipeline for two weeks.

Howe gave his full commitment to the club at the end of the season, but has changed his mind. He is set to take a break from football and Howe wanted the club to have a replacement lined up before he left.

This is Howe's decision, the club tried to convince him to stay. He feels he has taken it as far as he can after nearly five years at the helm.

There is no acrimony, the club love him and think he's done an amazing job.

The players have yet to be told. They are on a day off today. The squad fly out to Spain for a pre-season training camp on Friday. Newcastle are yet to comment or put out a statement.

This is not ideal timing as far as the club are concerned, but they are moving swiftly to try and replace Howe. They are in advanced talks with Jaissle of Al Alhi, having also spoken to Antonio Conte and Kieran McKenna.

'I cannot assure Bruno future' - Howe's final words as boss

In his final words as Newcastle boss, Howe refused to offer assurances over the future of captain Guimaraes amid heavy interest from Arsenal - but added the player is not in control of his own future.

Sky Sports News reported earlier this month that Guimaraes had told Newcastle he would like to leave the club in favour of a move to the Premier League champions, but the Magpies had no intention of selling the 28-year-old Brazil international.

Asked about Guimaraes, who is yet to rejoin his team-mates following the World Cup, Howe said on Wednesday night: "Assurances - I don't think you can push too hard for those. I think I've said many times you want players that are committed.

"Bruno's always been committed here. His training performances, his game performances, have been outstanding. Every time he's worn the shirt, he's played with the fans by his side. I'd love to see that continue.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look back at when Arsenal target Guimaraes took on the Gunners in a fiery clash at St James' Park in 2023

"I think we want to keep all of our best players. They're so valuable, and as I said numerous times, there aren't many of them, and to get them and develop them is so difficult.

"So when you have them, you want to keep them. And Bruno's very much in that category; he's an outstanding player."

Asked if this saga dragging on creates a negative mood, Howe replied: "Any distraction, if it's not healthy, is unhealthy. So, yeah.

"But we're not in control of that. And to some degree, I don't think Bruno's in control of that either.

"What will be, will be. We can't control the forces that are at play here, we've just got to make sure that when Bruno comes back, we look after him and he trains well, which I'm sure he will do. And he makes a difference as he always has done."

Bothroyd: Newcastle in relegation scrap without Howe

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Former Arsenal and England striker Jay Bothroyd worries for Newcastle following the departure of Howe and predicts they could end up in a relegation battle this season

Sky Sports News' Jay Bothroyd:

"There's so many players leaving, so to be honest I can understand why he [Howe] would want to leave now.

"He's saying: 'I had a strong squad. You've taken away some of the best players I had. Some of the best players in the Premier League. You're replacing them with unproven players in the Premier League.'

"It seems to me that he doesn't have the control he wants. He doesn't want to see these players leave.

"It's just really bad times for Newcastle, yet again. This is even worse than last year. Losing [Alexander] Isak and him not turning up to training is one thing, but now you're losing one of the best managers in the country and all your best players.

"Where do Newcastle go from here? It's going to be an unproven manager because who wants to put themselves in a situation where you don't have a strong side.

"I said mid-table [as a Premier League prediction]. Now I'm saying bottom half of the table.

"They're way off it. They're going to be in a relegation battle this year."

Your views on Howe's exit...

HullToon: I cannot believe it. Does he feel supported enough? Does the project still match the original plan that he set out for? There are so many questions raised because of this. Last season was disappointing, but there's mitigating circumstances.

JimmiDee: Regardless of last years disappointment, Howe has done an unbelievable job, and he's had to put up with his team being pillaged the last two seasons and expected to produce the same results with bargain bin replacements which is just completely unrealistic. He deserves better.

SPritc80: A section of our short sighted fans are to blame for Eddie leaving and some big hitters choosing to leave. Results have not gone our way at times. Jumping on the back of players and the head coach in the way they have is disrespectful. No wonder they are all leaving.

BrettJ2002: Why didn't Eddie Howe decide to do this before pre-season started so new manager can get a lot more time in with the squad? Thanks to Eddie for what he has done, but his time was definitely up.

Chris W: Strongly support Eddie - that's two new statues we need this month!

Fez71: Didn't look like Eddie was getting backed, selling all our best players. Very sad times, thanks for all the memories, Eddie.

Sports.title: Norrie into Los Cabos quarter-finals as Osaka advances in Washington
Sports.content:
Cameron Norrie continued his return to form at the Los Cabos Open by beating James Duckworth in straight sets to reach the quarter-finals.

Norrie had lost six successive matches across clay and grass before starting his summer hard-court campaign with victory over Aleksandar Kovacevic on Monday night.

The British No 2 backed up that performance with a 6-4 6-4 win over Duckworth on Wednesday evening to set up a last-eight clash with another Australian, Bernard Tomic.

Norrie lost his first service game of the match to fall 2-0 down, but would then claim two successive breaks of serve himself to take a 4-3 lead, before routinely closing the set out with a couple of holds.

The 30-year-old looked to be cruising to victory when he went up a double break in the second set to lead 5-2, but had to survive a brief wobble before getting over the line.

In the men's draw, Spanish teenager Rafael Jodar beat former champion Kei Nishikori to set up an exciting quarter-final clash with fourth seed Lorenzo Musetti.

On Thursday, all eyes will be on an all-Australian clash on the main stadium court as top seed Alex de Minaur takes on qualifier Cruz Hewitt, the 17-year-old son of former world No 1 Lleyton Hewitt.

Sports.title: Mullinax receives six-month ban for anti-doping violation
Sports.content:
Golfer Trey Mullinax has received a six-month ban after testing positive for a substance prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency.

Mullinax - whose one PGA Tour victory came at the 2022 Barbasol Championship - said in a statement provided by the Tour that he used a medication for a condition he was diagnosed with at university without seeking approval.

He becomes the ninth golfer to be suspended since the PGA Tour begin drug testing in 2008, and the first since Byeong Hun An was suspended for using a cough syrup that contained a prohibited substance in October 2023.

Image: Byeong Hun An was banned after using a cough syrup that contained a banned sustance

"It is my responsibility to understand and follow the PGA Tour's Anti-Doping Policy and all of its rules and regulations," Mullinax said in the statement. "I failed to do that, and that is on me.

"My lack of knowledge is not an excuse. It was my responsibility to know the rules before taking any medication and I failed to do so.

"I want to be absolutely clear: I have never taken any substance with the intention of gaining a competitive advantage.

Image: Trey Mullinax will be eligible to return on January 16

"Anyone who knows me knows how much I respect this game and the values it represents."

Mullinax has only appeared three times on the Tour this year, with one of those appearances coming at a Korn Ferry Tour event.

He finished 150th in the FedEx Cup last year, and has conditional status for the 2026 edition.

The American is eligible to return to the Tour on January 16, a week before the 2027 season begins.

Sports.title: Eddie Howe leaves Newcastle United with Matthias Jaissle set to replace him
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe has left Newcastle after losing control of transfers and is set to be replaced by the German coach Matthias Jaissle, who is in charge of the Saudi Arabian club Al-Ahli.

Although the timing of Howe’s abrupt departure following almost five years in charge at St James’ Park is unexpected, his position had been uncertain for some time. He is understood to have told Newcastle’s Saudi Arabian owners he wanted to leave more than a fortnight ago and the parting is said to be “amicable”.

Sources have suggested the 48-year-old told directors he was utterly drained and wanted to take a break from football following a transformative Tyneside tenure that saw Newcastle win the League Cup in 2025 and twice qualify for the Champions League.

In recent months Howe has become disillusioned after seeing his previously strong power-base and ability to dictate transfer policy diminished significantly. Already this summer Ross Wilson, the third sporting director of his managerial tenure, has presided over the sale of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali to Barcelona and Tottenham respectively. A year ago the team’s key striker Alexander Isak departed for Liverpool.

Quick Guide Howe's highs and lows at Newcastle Show 2021-22: The firefighter After taking over from Steve Bruce in November 2021, Eddie Howe gets strong backing in the January transfer window and guides Newcastle to an 11th-place finish. A run of six straight wins at home sees the Magpies become the first team in Premier League history to avoid relegation after failing to win any of their first 14 games.

2022-23: Return to Europe Alexander Isak arrives for big money in the summer, but it is mostly existing players like Callum Wilson and Miguel Almirón who power Howe's side to the League Cup final, which ends in defeat to Manchester United. Newcastle respond well, earning a fourth-place finish to qualify for the Champions League. 2023-24: Injuries bite Howe's training methods are called into doubt as Newcastle finish bottom of their Champions League group and struggle with injuries all season. They also lose £55m signing Sandro Tonali to a betting ban. A late run earns seventh spot but European hopes are dashed as Manchester United stun City in the FA Cup final. 2024-25: League Cup triumph A brilliant, Dan Burn-inspired win over Liverpool at Wembley sees Howe lift the League Cup (pictured) and finally end Newcastle's long trophy drought. With Isak banging in 23 Premier League goals, the Toon secure a fifth-place finish, which is good enough to earn Champions League qualification once again. 2025-26: The ghost of Isak A summer-long saga over the sale of Isak to Liverpool scuppers plans for Howe's fourth full season in charge. The fans turn on wantaway Anthony Gordon midway through a campaign that is all but ended by a humiliating 7-2 defeat at Barcelona in March. Howe's final five months in charge feature 14 defeats across all competitions as Newcastle slump to 12th in the Premier League. Tom Bassam Photograph: Danny Lawson/PA Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Not that Howe gave any indication of the events about to unfold when he spoke to reporters following Wednesday night’s 4-1 pre season friendly defeat at Bristol City. “Every day as Newcastle manager is a great day for me,” he said. “I absolutely love the football club and that will never change. There has been a lot of change at the football club and potentially more to come. [But] I think there’s always reasons to be optimistic. I believe great things are possible every season. I see no reason for it be any different this year.”On ThursdayYesterday morning the Newcastle hierarchy’s negotiations with Jaissle were said to be at an advanced stage and the club’s players had a day off interrupted by news that that there would be a change of manager. Given that Al-Ahli are also owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, Jaissle’s split from his club is unlikely to prove problematic.

The 38-year-old had a brief playing career as a defender with Hoffenheim and has been in charge of Al-Ahli since 2023, presiding over 90 wins, 25 draws and 23 defeats. Along the way he has won a Saudi Super Cup and two Asian Champions Leagues. At RB Salzburg he won the Austrian Cup.

Although a disappointing 12th placed Premier League finish last season left some Newcastle fans calling for Howe’s dismissal, the former Bournemouth manager appeared to have convinced PIF to offer him another chance during a high level summit meeting at a Northumberland country house hotel in April. He is understood to have reiterated his commitment to the job after returning from holiday in June but subsequently became disenchanted by the events of a turbulent summer.

Quite apart from the exits of Gordon and Tonali it has featured considerable doubt surrounding the future of the Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimaraes who is coveted by Arsenal. At Bristol City on Wednesday night, Howe admitted he had “lost control” of transfers and did not know whether Guimaraes would board the team’s flight to South east Spain ahead of a training Camp at La Manga on Friday.

While Guimaraes is understood to have told Newcastle he wants to join Arsenal this summer, Howe had developed increasing reservations about a new, PIF approved, policy of signing largely young players with high resale potential, priced, broadly, in the £20m to £40m bracket. With Newcastle operating under a Uefa settlement agreement, Wilson believes it is the best way to remain within football’s spending rules.

View image in fullscreen Eddie Howe oversaw a 4-1 friendly defeat to Bristol City on Wednesday, in what proved to be his final game in charge. Photograph: David Davies/PA

So far this summer the sporting director has recruited four promising yet inexperienced players aged 20 or under in Ewen Jaouen, Bazoumana Toure, Aladji Bamba and Sean Steur. Howe feared expectations raised earlier this year when his chief executive David Hopkinson claimed that by 2030 he wanted Newcastle to “be in the conversation” about the identity of the best clubs in the world. The outgoing manager told friends things “no longer felt right.”

Although Howe acquired a number of critics as results, increasingly, disappointed last season, he will long be remembered with affection and gratitude at St James’ Park. After succeeding Steve Bruce as manager in November 2021 he led Newcastle to two Carabao Cup finals and in winning the second - against Liverpool - last year secured the club’s first significant domestic silverware for 70 years.

With his assistant, Jason Tindall, also expected to leave, the squad are likely to be placed under the caretaker charge of first team coach, Graeme Jones, for the flight to La Manga.

The club hope that Jaissle will soon join them. With the former Nottingham Forest manager Vitor Pereira poised to replace him at Al-Ahli, the expectations is that the German will take the helm well before Newcastle’s training camp concludes with a pre-season friendly at Valencia on Saturday 8 August.

Alan Shearer has been taken aback by the change’s timeline. “I’m very, very surprised,” said the club’s former captain and manager. “It’s strange timing with three weeks to go until the new season. I don’t know what’s gone on but I’m led to believe it was Eddie’s decision to leave. He did a wonderful job so it’s a huge thank you to Eddie.”

Sports.title: Fifa ‘undermining the very foundations of football’, says AFC as Uefa talks loom
Sports.content:
The Asian Football Confederation has accused Fifa of undermining the foundations of football by failing to consult the confederations over their plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

In a letter sent on Thursday by president Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa to AFC’s 47 members, which has been seen by the Guardian, Fifa’s unilateral actions in doing a deal with Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Capital to buy 20% of a new company that would control the commercial rights of all global tournaments is roundly condemned.

Al-Khalifa’s intervention appears significant, as the AFC has previously been strong supporters of Gianni Infantino and has already pledged to vote for him en masse in next year’s Fifa presidential election.

With the South American confederation Conmebol and the Confederation of African Football (Caf) firmly behind Infantino the AFC’s position is critical, as they appear to have the balance of power.

Uefa and the North American confederation Concacaf have both strongly opposed the sell-off, but with just 65 votes between them would not have sufficient numbers to block Fifa’s proposal, which requires a simple majority of their 211 to pass.

The AFC had issued a statement echoing Uefa’s concerns over governance yesterday, but al-Khalifa’s letter goes further.

“The AFC notes with great concern and disappointment that it was not consulted by Fifa at any level prior to the public announcement of this proposal, and nor has it received any detailed governance, financial or legal analysis of the proposal and its potential repercussions, which is totally unacceptable,” he wrote.

“Furthermore, the AFC is deeply concerned that Fifa’s unilateral actions appear to undermine the very foundations of continental football, which are based on solidarity, cooperation and transparency. Moreover, such an initiative will not succeed without the support of all the confederations, which is not the case now.”

Al-Khalifa also called on Fifa to alter their timetable after Infantino gave national associations a deadline of 19 September to decide whether to accept an initial payment of $20m (£15m) that would be generated by the sale.

“The AFC is surprised that the current timeline allows an extremely limited period for consideration of a proposal of such significance, when such decisions should never be rushed, and it is imperative that all factors be considered and debated,” he wrote.

“The AFC firmly believes that sufficient time must be afforded for a comprehensive assessment, including appropriate legal and governance due diligence, meaningful consultation and careful consideration of the long-term implications of such an initiative.

“Above all, it is essential that the appropriate Fifa bodies be involved in the decision-making process and that the matter is handled at all times in accordance with the Fifa Statutes and the highest standards of ethics and good governance.”

Uefa will hold an emergency ­meeting of its 55 members on Thursday afternoon to discuss their next steps, with a senior source telling the Guardian on Thursday morning that a boycott of Fifa tournaments would be the main discussion point.

Sports.title: Chelsea complete deal for Crystal Palace and France defender Maxence Lacroix
Sports.content:
Maxence Lacroix has joined Chelsea from Crystal Palace to become the club’s fifth signing of the summer so far. The France international, who won the FA Cup and Conference League with Palace, has been the Blues’ main defensive target of the window.

Lacroix, 26, signs a six-year deal with Xabi Alonso’s side. “I am really happy to be part of this beautiful club,” said Lacroix, who played three times for France at the World Cup, including in their 6-4 bronze medal match defeat to England.

“Everyone knows the legend of Chelsea, its tradition of winning, and to be a part of that is a proud moment. I think it’s the best move for me because it’s the best club in the world. When I spoke with the manager, I saw that we have the same direction and desire for this club.

“We want to win. When you see the quality of the players here, everything we have around the club, it’s something that we can achieve. The ambition is to lift trophies, and I can’t wait to contribute.”

Chelsea had been looking to add experience to their back line having missed out on Rennes’ Jeremy Jacquet in January, with the player opting to join Liverpool. Levi Colwill, who is considered to be a key part of the club’s long-term plans, missed almost all of last season with an anterior cruciate ligament injury, with Wesley Fofana and Trevoh Chalobah forming the central-defensive partnership for much of the campaign.

After a dismal season that saw the club finish 10th, the club’s hierarchy has acknowledged a change in recruitment policy is needed, with a refocusing away from young, inexperienced players towards ones that can help the team compete for the title.

Lacroix, who made 55 appearances last season for Palace, has been one of the league’s most consistent defenders since moving to Selhurst Park from Wolfsburg in 2024.

The Blues confirmed the club-record arrival of Aston Villa forward Morgan Rogers last week, and have also added Atalanta defender Marco Palestra, striker Emmanuel Emegha from Strasbourg and Sporting Lisbon’s Geovany Quenda.

Sports.title: WSL fixtures: London City Lionesses open 2026-27 season against Manchester United
Sports.content:
Those desperate to see what London City Lionesses will look like with two-time Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas in their ranks do not have to wait long, with the big-spending club kicking off the new Women’s Super League season against Manchester United on Friday 4 September.

The Michelle Kang-owned side welcome United to Hayes Lane in the first game of the 2026-27 season, which will also likely feature goalkeeper Mary Earps, who returns to the WSL for an opener against her former club after leaving Paris Saint-Germain to join London City this summer.

The full fixture list for the new season has been announced, and comes after an extremely complex scheduling process, with WSL Football running more that 1.5 billion scheduling iterations as it juggles the stadium availability and broadcast windows following the announcement of the calendars and fixtures of the Premier League, EFL and men’s National League and men’s FA Cup, women’s FA Cup, Carabao Cup, and men’s and women’s Champions League.

Also on the opening weekend, WSL champions Manchester City, who have added the former Arsenal forward Beth Mead and Chelsea defender Niamh Charles to their ranks, begin their title defence against WSL2 champions Birmingham. The Midlands side were promoted alongside Charlton and Crystal Palace with the top flight expanding to 14 teams for the first time.

Arsenal start their campaign against Brighton, who knocked them out of the FA Cup at the quarter-final stage shortly before they earned a draw in the league against the Gunners that handed Manchester City their first title since 2016.

Elsewhere, Charlton, who earned a playoff win over Leicester to earn their promotion at the expense of the WSL’s bottom-placed side, will play Liverpool at home, Tottenham host West Ham, Chelsea welcome Aston Villa to Stamford Bridge and Crystal Palace mark their return to the WSL against Everton.

Sports.title: Experimental Liverpool down Wrexham thanks to Rio Ngumoha’s winner
Sports.content:
Liverpool turned the Empire State Building red when launching a new away kit on Tuesday but neither they nor Wrexham could illuminate Yankee Stadium 24 hours later. It was rough in the diamond, although Rio Ngumoha’s deflected goal made it two wins out of two for Andoni Iraola on his first pre-season tour as Liverpool head coach.

Ngumoha, a second half substitute who Iraola deployed on the right, satisfied the majority of a 42,204 crowd with a 75th-minute shot that looped in off Wrexham defender Lewis Brunt. Wrexham’s Hollywood co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney (now simply Rob Mac) were in attendance for what the former had labelled a “punch-me moment” but in truth few blows were traded at the iconic baseball stadium.

Liverpool’s preparations for the second game of pre-season were not exactly smooth, in fairness to Iraola’s team. Their flight from Chicago was cancelled on Tuesday night with players and staff on the tarmac ready to take off. Poor weather conditions in the New York area delayed their arrival until the day of the game, and Liverpool only checked into their Midtown hotel around midday. They were flying back to Chicago straight after the match too.

Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch did not make the trip from Liverpool’s training base despite joining up with the squad following their post-World Cup holidays. The game came too early in their pre-season preparations to be considered. With Joe Gomez injured and Federico Chiesa also absent through illness, Iraola had little choice but to select another young and experimental side. Six of Liverpool’s starting line-up had no Premier League experience whatsoever but at least the emphasis on youth offered the crowd a glimpse of the highly-rated Joshua Abe.

View image in fullscreen Joshua Abe reacts after failing to score at Yankee Stadium. Photograph: Angela Weiss/AFP/Getty Images

Abe, a pacy and prolific right winger, is regarded as one of the brightest prospects in the country and was inundated with offers before committing his future to Liverpool when turning 16 earlier this month. Manchester City, Manchester United and Chelsea were all interested in the Warrington-born England youth international, with deals worth £40,000-a-week reportedly on his table. There was understandable relief inside Anfield when he agreed scholarship terms in June with a three-year professional contract to follow on his 17th birthday next July.

Abe could have marked his first senior Liverpool start with an early goal when released clear of the Wrexham defence by Harvey Elliott. A heavy first touch gave the Wrexham and former Liverpool goalkeeper Danny Ward opportunity to save at the feet of the teenager. Iraola started with a front line of Calum Scanlon, Lewis Koumas and Abe. Koumas went close from distance and had a penalty shout waved away but, aside from a few surging midfield runs by Dominik Szoboszlai, it was a quiet friendly.

Wrexham are further along in their pre-season work – their first competitive game is a week on Friday against Middlesbrough in the Carabao Cup – and it showed as the first half progressed and Phil Parkinson’s team gained a physical edge. Sam Smith and Callum Doyle were unable to trouble Giorgi Mamardashvili with the chances that fell their way.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Abe, Scanlon, Milos Kerkez and Trey Nyoni were replaced at half-time by Ngumoha, Kieran Morrison, Kostas Tsimikas and Curtis Jones respectively. Elliott was presented with a sight of the Wrexham goal by Koumas minutes after the restart but his first-time shot from 20 yards was well saved by Ward. The Wales international also denied Szoboszlai from distance but this was a Liverpool performance – and pre-season friendly – that failed to ignite.

Wrexham substitute Nathan Broadhead almost succeeded with a powerful drive from 25 yards that was pushed away by Mamardashvili. Brunt and Kieffer Moore both had good late chances to equalise but miscued from close range.

Sports.title: England’s 1966 World Cup heroes were fun, humble and unlike today’s stars
Sports.content:
With each passing World Cup I am reminded of the times I spent in the company of those wonderful “Boys of 66”. What a privilege it was getting to know them in a much simpler era when, unlike today’s mollycoddled stars, household names remained unaffected by money and fame.

Where were you on 30 July 1966, the day England won the World Cup? I was at my nan and grandad’s house. They had a minute television which seemed no bigger than a matchbox. Intermittently the picture, which was in black and white, would roll around the screen. It was infuriating. My grandad talked about needing to get the “horizontal hold fixed” (unless you are of a certain age you will need to Google that). I was nine years old.

Thirty years (of hurt) on from that final, there was a knock at my front door. It was a surreal experience to see Geoff Hurst standing on my doorstep and even more bizarre as he went to one end of my front room and stood behind the settee. I went to the other end and sat on a chair.

Geoff, England’s World Cup hat- trick hero, had come to my house to rehearse his after-dinner speech. The settee acted as a makeshift top table. I was the only member of his audience.

His performance began. “I was at Paddington station one day and a chap came running up to me and said, ‘Geoff, Geoff, I’ve been waiting 20 years to meet you, I know exactly where I was that day in 1966 when you scored your hat-trick.’ ‘Where was that?’ asked Geoff. ‘Pentonville prison,’ replied the man. ‘We were so happy we smashed the cell up.’”

I had written some of Geoff’s script and I helped him with his presentation, but he quickly became a natural performer.

Another of Geoff’s stories provides a fascinating insight into how the manager, Alf Ramsey, made sure his players never became complacent. In one England match Hurst played in, after the World Cup final, the players returned to the team hotel. They said their goodbyes and Hurst turned to Ramsey and said: “See you next time Alf.”

“Perhaps, Geoff, perhaps,” replied Ramsey. Geoff said it was a comment that really made him think that, despite scoring a hat-trick, his place wasn’t guaranteed.

Ramsey’s starting salary as England manager was £4,500 a year rising to a maximum of £5,000. He also asked the Football Association to help him buy a house.

In the 1980s, and for many years afterwards, there was a huge circuit of sporting dinners. They were often in the north of England and held at the traditional working men’s clubs. Many of the 1966 England team were regular performers. Unlike today’s Premier League stars, who earn hundreds of thousands of pounds a month the “Boys of 66” supplemented their income by performing on the circuit, which is where I got to know them.

View image in fullscreen Bobby Charlton raises the Jules Rimet trophy in the air after the 1966 final at Wembley. Photograph: Hulton Archive/Getty Images

Sometimes they would do their own routines, on other occasions I would interview them and tee them up for their anecdotes. On stage one night I said to Jack Charlton: “Jack, how’s your brother Bobby?” Bobby could sometimes be very serious and he didn’t smile very often. “Not great” replied Jack. “Oh, why’s that?” I enquired. “Well, he’s now been banned from his local pub, the landlord said he didn’t want him there during the happy hour.”

Those England players were involved in English sport’s greatest day but you would never have known. They didn’t act like unapproachable superstars. If I left a message on their home answerphone they would call straight back. It was so different to the majority of football personalities I tried to interview in later years for the BBC.

Some of the events I worked at with the 1966 team were for amateur football clubs. We would be part of the entertainment alongside a tribute act, or a local comedian. The evening would sometimes start with a game of bingo. One dinner was very different. I was asked by the Institute of Directors to host a show and book as many of the England team as possible for a corporate lunch in London. I waited in the green room and they started filling in. It was like being in a dream and I imagined I was in the Wembley dressing room. In they trooped: George Cohen, Ray Wilson, Nobby Stiles, Hurst, Roger Hunt, Alan Ball, Martin Peters, Bobby and Jack Charlton, and for good measure BBC TV’s Kenneth Wolstenholme, who delivered the greatest commentary line in the history of sports broadcasting.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Stiles was a great raconteur. One of his favourite anecdotes was based around the game England played against Argentina in the quarter-final. Before the match, Nobby, the hard man of the team, was taken to one side by Ramsey. “Nobby, Argentina’s best player is Antonio Rattín, I want you to mark Rattín,” said Ramsey. After a perfectly timed pause Nobby delivered the punchline: “Alf, do you want me to mark him for the match or for his entire life?”

View image in fullscreen England’s manager Alf Ramsey (left) celebrates his team’s 4-2 victory over West Germany with the captain, Bobby Moore, and Nobby Stiles. Photograph: Keystone/Getty Images

It was a story that brought the house down.

In 1982 I was asked by Ian Thomas, my editor at BBC Radio Sport, to meet Ramsey at Liverpool Street station. Ramsey had been booked by the BBC to give his reaction to the draw for the 1982 World Cup finals. He immediately reminded me of Captain Mainwaring from Dad’s Army. He spoke with a posh voice, in clipped tones, and came across as a very serious man. I was just 24 years old, and I couldn’t believe my luck.

These were very different times. I still find it incredible that, on the morning of the 1966 final, Peters told me that, “time seemed to be dragging” so some of the players went shopping on Hendon’s high street. And after England’s win at Wembley the FA arranged an evening banquet for the players but, astonishingly, their wives were not invited. The players were very angry and when the dinner finished Hurst told me that he and several of the other players and their wives headed to Danny La Rue’s cabaret club.

How times have changed and how lucky was I knowing the 1966 team? They were humble and really fun to be with and I still find it incredible that I spent so many great times with them.

Garry Richardson presents a special 1966 World Cup anniversary programme on Boom Radio on 30 July

Sports.title: Fifa opens disciplinary proceedings against Argentina over Falklands banner and final chaos
Sports.content:
Fifa has opened disciplinary ­proceedings against Argentina over the Falkland Islands banner ­displayed after their World Cup semi‑final win against England in Atlanta.

As Argentina celebrated ­reaching the final with their dramatic 2-1 ­victory, several players held a sign ­proclaiming “Las Malvinas son ­Argentinas” – the ­Malvinas are Argentinian – in ­reference to the ­British overseas territory in the south Atlantic.

The dispute over the islands, which have been ruled by Britain since 1833, is long running and led to a 74-day conflict in 1982, during which more than 900 people – 649 Argentinians and 255 Britons – lost their lives.

Fifa’s disciplinary code ­prohibits “using a sports event for ­demonstrations of a non-sporting nature” and the banner prompted political debate on both sides of the ­Atlantic. A spokesperson for the then UK prime minister, Keir Starmer, said: “The World Cup might not be ours, but the Falkland Islands ­definitely are.” Andrew Giuliani, the head of the White House Fifa taskforce, defended Argentina’s players, saying the US believed in free speech.

The incident was not the first time an Argentina team had expressed such sentiments. In 2014, Fifa fined Argentina £20,000 for a far larger banner held ‌up by players before a friendly with Slovenia in La Plata.

Fifa’s full World Cup charge sheet against the Argentinian Football Association also includes ­“discriminatory chants and gestures, late kick-offs, failure to comply with match and security protocols, the display of inappropriate messages by the team and spectators and the throwing of objects by spectators in relation to several matches”.

0:18 Ugly scenes as Argentina lose World Cup final – video

Several players are also under investigation in relation to the ­chaotic scenes that followed ­Argentina’s 1-0 extra-time defeat by Spain in the final. As Spain attempted to celebrate, ­altercations broke out across the pitch at New York New Jersey Stadium.

The Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes, who was seen wrestling Spain’s Eric García to the ground, faces three counts of assault under the Fifa disciplinary code, while the defender Nahuel Molina faces two counts of assault (one completed and one attempted) and one count of unsporting behaviour.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The assistant coach, Roberto Ayala, faces one count of assault, and Thiago Almada, an unused substitute in the final, one count of unsporting behaviour. Spain’s Gavi also faces an unsporting behaviour charge.

“In accordance with the Fifa ­disciplinary code, the respondents have now been provided with the opportunity to present their position, following which a decision will be issued by the Fifa disciplinary committee in due course,” said Fifa.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Jack Grealish to make Saudi switch to Al-Hilal?
Sports.content:
Having been left behind like an unloved t-shirt by Enzo Maresca as Manchester City departed for their pre-season tour of Asia, Jack Grealish is attracting admiring glances from elsewhere. Eyeing up the England attacker’s shapely calves are Al-Hilal of the Saudi Pro League, who would certainly have the funds to fulfil City’s desire of slapping a big ‘SOLD’ sticker on Grealish and preparing him for international shipping.

The latest highly-touted prospect set to be whisked away after an impressive short stint at Bournemouth is Rayan. Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, PSG, Arsenal, and Liverpool all want the Brazilian winger. The link with Andoni Iraola at Anfield appears strong, but with the 19-year-old’s release clause not said to kick in until 2027, the fee required to move him from the south coast would be significant. Although probably still less than the price of a Bradley Barcola.

There’s been more outs than ins at Crystal Palace this summer and that looks set to continue after a move for Augsburg’s Chrislain Matsima stalled. The French defender, 24, had been lined up as the replacement for Maxence Lacroix, who is on the verge of being shown Jordan Henderson’s magic tricks at Chelsea.

Inter Milan’s remarkably coherent cohort of cast-offs could well be joined by Curtis Jones. The Liverpool midfielder has been consistently linked with the Serie A club this summer, but the sticking point appears to be price. The Reds rejected a £21.5m offer back in June and were said to be seeking closer to £35m for the 25-year-old. With Inter potentially saving some of their transfer kitty earmarked for Cristian Romero by instead moving for free agent John Stones, they may be able to find a little more cash down the back of the sofa to return to Liverpool with a revised bid.

Aston Villa have a few readies burning a hole in their pocket after trousering £117m for Morgan Rogers, and want to spend some of it on a Brazilian striker named after a Surrey golf club member, Allan of Palmeiras. Villa have gone in with a £26m offer for the 22-year-old but the São Paulo club think they can extract a bit more than that – at least £12m more, in fact.

Danny Welbeck’s impending arrival at Cobham looks likely to push Liam Delap down the pecking order at Chelsea and Everton are “ready to revive” their interest. The Toffees have been persistent in suggesting they would like to offer the 23-year-old a platform to reboot his career, and may now actually do something about it.

Another Englishman looking for an upturn in fortunes is Kalvin Phillips, who remarkably is still officially on the books at Manchester City. Last season the midfielder spent some time on loan at Sheffield United and it seems that worked well for everyone, as the Blades want to bring the Yorkshire-born metronome back to Bramall Lane.

Sports.title: Up to his old clicks? Local 'Clicky Ponting' cricket player at centre of 'cheat' row 'used same ploy at previous club'
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The 'Clicky Ponting' scandal gripping amateur cricket has spread across Yorkshire following claims that the man behind it began cheating at a second club five years ago.

Brian Devine, whose club Saltburn CC is facing a corruption investigation, has been caught on camera attempting to mislead umpires during a game for his previous side, Pudsey St Lawrence.

Footage of a Bradford Premier League match from August 2021 shows him repeatedly clicking his fingers while opponents are batting, in an apparent effort to mimic the sound of a ball hitting the bat.

At the time, Devine was captain of Pudsey St Lawrence's second XI. On the day in question, his side restricted their opponents New Farnley to 136 runs in a rain-affected game they eventually lost.

The team came third in the league that year, and fourth in 2022, before winning the title in Devine's final season at the club. As skipper, he was photographed on the club's social media feeds brandishing a large trophy.

Only a tiny number of matches were filmed at the time. But statistics survive showing that during the three seasons Devine captained Pudsey St Lawrence its second XI wicketkeeper Jacob McDonald took 96 catches, an average of 32 per year.

Devine then returned to Saltburn, his childhood club, in 2024 after taking a job as company secretary to a livestock auctioneer in Northallerton.

In the two years that followed his departure, McDonald took 22 and 15 catches respectively. So far this season, he's managed just five.

Brian Devine was caught repeatedly clicking his fingers while opponents were batting, in an apparent effort to mimic the sound of a ball hitting the bat

Footage from 2021 shows Devine attempting to mislead umpires during a game for his previous side Pudsey St Lawrence

Footage of Devine flamboyantly clicking his fingers five years ago, which was uncovered by the Daily Mail yesterday, has sparked calls for the Bradford Premier League to mount a formal investigation.

Sources at other clubs now believe umpires in the league, which was founded in 1902, were for years being routinely misled into ruling that opposing batsmen had touched the ball and been caught by McDonald.

'Our lads have been looking back at surviving film and score books and we have come to the conclusion that he's been at it for years,' said a source at one rival club.

'Young players will have lost opportunities because of this, match results will have undoubtedly been affected, and there is a good case for now stripping Pudsey St Lawrence of its 2023 title.

'Devine was a highly competitive and quite bumptious captain, and the bigger question is of course what club staff and his team-mates did or didn't know about his antics.'

Bradford Premier League officials were not returning calls last night. But a finding of wrongdoing would send shockwaves through Yorkshire cricket.

Pudsey St Lawrence, which was founded in 1845, is one of the most venerable teams in club cricket and produced two of Yorkshire and England's greatest ever players: Herbert Sutcliffe, who averaged more than 60 in Test matches, and Sir Leonard Hutton, who scored 368 against Australia in 1938.

Martin Reed, Chairperson at Pudsey St Lawrence Cricket Club, told the Daily Mail: 'We were not aware of any issues with Mr Devine's behaviour during his time at the club, nor were concerns raised with us by other clubs or officials.

'Had we been made aware of any issues at the time we would have taken appropriate action.

'It is some time since Mr Devine left Pudsey St Lawrence and we are aware that the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League and Saltburn Cricket Club are currently investigating the matter.'

Sports.title: Love Island star Gemma Owen finishes fourth as she rides in her first ever race - watched by her proud father Michael at Goodwood
Sports.content:
Love Island star Gemma Owen finishes fourth as she rides in her first ever race - watched by her proud father Michael at Goodwood

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Gemma Owen missed out on claiming her first win in jockey's silks as she finished fourth in ladies-only charity race the Markel Magnolia Cup at Goodwood Festival on Thursday.

Owen started out wide on the near side and lost ground in the early stages but as the pack neared the post, gained impressively on her rivals.

But there was no touching the winner Imaan Rasul-Healer, a Newmarket insider, who rode the renamed Khor Al Adaid to victory by some distance.

Rasul-Healer had been the race's first reserve until this week, when racing reporter Molly Hunter was forced to withdraw after an attack of vertigo.

Gemma's dad Michael, the former England and Liverpool striker, was watching on and told Daily Mail Sport: ‘It was quite strange, nerve racking obviously worrying about her safety, albeit she’s a very capable rider.

‘However, going 40mph on the back of a horse is never the safest thing to do.

‘She missed the start by quite a long way which was frustrating as we all know how important the start is and she was told a hundred times, but she rode well so it’s all good.

‘I have a suspicion this won’t be her last ride in public as she has thoroughly loved the process, and they have lady amateur races so Hugo (Palmer) was already talking to her a week or two ago about perhaps riding in those.

‘I’d say she’s as competitive as me, so she won’t be happy she’s been beaten. She was left miles at the start, but I hope she still enjoyed the experience.'

Gemma Owen came fourth in her first race as a jockey as she took part in the Magnolia Cup

The ladies-only charity race is run on Ladies' Day at Goodwood Festival and brings together aspiring jockeys and novices alike

Owen was watched by her famous father Michael as she put in a promising performance

The Love Island star is a passionate equestrian and has shared her love of horses with her 1.6 million Instagram followers.

Owen's background however is in dressage, and as Owen said ahead of taking part in the race, her experience as a jockey was nil.

'I’m really looking forward to taking part in the Markel Magnolia Cup this year,' Owen said.

'Believe it or not, I had never sat on a racehorse until a couple of months ago and the training so far has been humbling to say the least.'

'Spending more time at Manor House Stables, seeing how a racing yard runs like clockwork and getting out onto the gallops, has been an incredible experience.

'It is an even bigger challenge than I initially expected but I'm excited to take part in such a prestigious fundraising event which raises so much money for charities supporting women and children.'

Manor House Stables is the enterprise run by her football legend father Michael, who set up the yard in 2006.

Michael and his wife Louise Bonsall were both in attendance to watch their daughter compete, as well as to take in a number of runners on the Festival's Ladies' Day.

Winner Imaan Rasul-Healer ran a formidable race on Khor Al Adaid to claim Thursday's win

Phantom Watch - running for the day as Turbo Trotter - was Owen's mount, but Manor House Stables also have Lion Of Alba, Adaay Of Scarlett, High Hazard, Mia Fantasia, and Mr Seagull running throughout Day Three.

Among Owen's fellow jockeys were a slew of inspirational women, intent on raising funds for the Cup's chosen charities, Education Above All Foundation and Educate A Child International.

Those connected with the racing world included Australian racehorse trainer and broadcaster Charlotte Littlefield and bloodstock agent Victoria Wang.

Racing charity Riding A Dream Academy has fielded young jockey Ruth Inman, while a number of those newer to the sport - including Royal Marsden Hospital microsurgeon Joanna Bovis and Real Housewives of Cheshire star and breast cancer survivor Nermina Pieters-Mekic - also took part.

Sports.title: Five stewards charged with assault after Man United fan, 49, was allegedly attacked at Old Trafford after draw with Man City last year
Sports.content:
Five stewards have been charged with assault after a Manchester United fan was allegedly attacked at Old Trafford following the Manchester derby last year.

The men are accused of assaulting a 49-year-old supporter in the East Stand during a sit-in protest following the goalless draw with Manchester City in April 2025.

Mohammed Jamil Akbar, 22, Yaseen Islam, 24, and Mohammed Uzair Iqbal, 24, all from Oldham, Favour Stevenson, 28, from Rochdale, and Usman Hussain, 36, from Manchester, have been charged with assault occasioning actual bodily harm and are due to appear at Manchester Magistrates’ Court on January 7 next year.

None of the five men charged were working for United and were employed by Controlled Solutions Group, a security company contracted by the club on match days. United and CSG declined to comment.

The protest was organised as a show of opposition to the club’s decision to increase season-ticket prices and scrap concessions for OAPs and children.

United’s ticketing policy has come under fire again in recent days over a clampdown on touting that has led to thousands of fans receiving emails saying their accounts have been suspended due to suspicious activity and their season tickets could be revoked unless they provide a satisfactory explanation.

Five stewards have been charged with assault after a Manchester United fan was allegedly attacked at Old Trafford following the Manchester derby last year

The incident came after a goalless draw between Man City and Man United in April 2025 (pictured above - an action shot from the game)

A number of supporters’ groups joined forces last week to issue a statement accusing the club of making innocent fans feel as though they are being ‘treated as suspects’ and adopting a ‘ban first and ask questions later’ approach.

On Wednesday, the Manchester United Muslims Supporters’ Club said there is a ‘feeling that Manchester United is becoming increasingly disconnected from the people who built the club’.

Sports.title: Atletico Madrid reignite interest in Tottenham captain Cristian Romero - plus the latest on Marcus Rashford's Manchester United future following Roma links: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid reignite interest in Tottenham captain Cristian Romero - plus the latest on Marcus Rashford's Manchester United future following Roma links: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Fredricson moves on

Manchester United defender Tyler Fredricson has agreed a permanent move to Swiss club Lausanne-Sport, subject to registration.

Fredricson made four first-team appearances since he was handed a debut against Wolves in 2025 – when he also won the reserve-team player of the year award – and was on the bench on a number of occasions last season.

United have inserted a substantial sell-on clause and a buy-back clause into the deal.

The 21-year-old, who joined United at Under-9 level, played in every round of United’s successful FA Youth Cup campaign in 2022 until illness ruled him out of the final against Nottingham Forest.

The club confirmed Fredricson’s departure in a statement on Thursday, saying: ‘Everybody at United thanks Tyler for all his efforts during his time with the club and we wish him all the best for the next chapter of his career.’

Fredricson joins United loanee Sekou Kone at the Swiss Super League side.

CHRIS WHEELER

Rashford says no to Roma

Marcus Rashford has no interest in joining Roma this summer as speculation regarding his future grows.

The 28-year-old is set to report to pre-season training with Manchester United in the coming days after returning from his loan spell with Barcelona.

Roma had been one of several clubs linked with a move for the England attacker, but Daily Mail Sport understands a move to the Italian giants does not appeal.

Fulham to spend big on Garcia

Fulham are closing on agreement with Real Madrid over a deal worth £35m for striker Gonzalo Garcia. The deal also includes £2m in bonuses and matching rights.

Madrid have been discussing a buy-back option and a 30 per cent sell-on clause as talks draw to a conclusion.

Fulham also working to add midfielder Cesar Palacios on loan from Madrid.

Gonzalo Garcia looks set to join Fulham from Real Madrid in a deal worth £60m

Hull's Nobel quest

Hull are advancing in talks for Rayo Vallecano defender Nobel Mendy.

As Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday, Hull had made enquiries and proposed a £15m offer for the 21-year-old who can play centre back and left back.

Rangers tried to sign Mendy a year ago from Real Betis but Vallecano got him for £2.5m and a 20 per cent sell-on clause.

Hull face competition from Ipswich for Burnley's Florentino Luis but have enquired about Augsburg's midfielder Mert Komur.

Coventry explore Hamer homecoming

Coventry City are exploring a deal to re-sign Gustavo Hamer from Sheffield United.

The 29-year-old midfielder has one year left on his deal at Bramall Lane.

The Brazilian made 132 appearances for the club scoring 19 goals which included a strike in the Championship play-off final against Luton Town at Wembley.

Atletico reignite Romero interest

Atletico Madrid have rekindled their interest in Tottenham defender Cristian Romero.

The Argentina international's agents held talks with Inter Milan last weekend and director Piero Ausilio confirmed interest but that the deal would be complicated owing to the financial package.

Atletico Madrid are exploring a potential move for Tottenham captain Cristian Romero

Atletico had interest last year and are exploring the figures involved in a deal for the 28-year-old Spurs captain again.

Inter are in the market for centre backs this summer, with one new recruit expected to be John Stones if all goes to plan in his medical today.

Stones set for Inter switch

England defender John Stones has arrived in Italy ahead of his medical with Inter Milan.

Stones, 32, left Manchester City at the end of last season following 10 years with the club.

"Sono entusiasta di essere qui". John Stones è arrivato a Milano ⚫️🔵 pic.twitter.com/Xp2rS66VL9 — Fcinter1908 (@fcin1908it) July 30, 2026

Meanwhile, talks between Manchester City and Lille are reaching a crucial stage over the transfer of Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The 18-year-old Morocco international is ready to make the move now though his club have been keen to keep him in France for another season as part of negotiations.

City are ready to use him this season with Rodri a target for Real Madrid while interest is building in Nico Gonzalez and Tijjani Reijnders.

City have lost Bernardo Silva and also have interest from Tottenham in Omar Marmoush and Savinho.

Bouaddi was valued around £60m before the World Cup but is now considered to be worth around £80m.

City also want to add another goalkeeper to replace Leeds-bound James Trafford with Marseille's Geronimo Rulli one name under consideration. They also want to strengthen at right-back and on the wing with Chelsea's Pedro Neto and Paris St Germain's Ibrahim Mbaye among names discussed.

Sports.title: Newcastle legend Alan Shearer reveals his shock at Eddie Howe's exit and predicts club will have to 'navigate tough waves' this season
Sports.content:
Newcastle legend Alan Shearer reveals his shock at Eddie Howe's exit and predicts club will have to 'navigate tough waves' this season

Alan Shearer admitted he was very surprised by the 'strange timing' of Eddie Howe's Newcastle departure and revealed he is 'led to believe it was Eddie's decision to leave' the Magpies just three weeks before the start of the Premier League season.

Speaking exclusively to Betfair, the Newcastle legend gave his immediate reaction to Howe leaving the club.

He said: 'If something was going to happen, you would have thought it would have happened at the end of last season so it would have given Newcastle time to prepare.'

'I don't know what's gone on, whether it was the end of last season, whether it was the summer, whether he feels they can't continue to sell his best players.

'I don't think it's a great look for what's happening at the minute with Newcastle. We're selling all our best players. The fans are seeing Isak go, the fans are seeing Tonali go, the fans are seeing Gordon go. My guess is it's probably only a matter of time before Bruno goes.'

Despite the sudden switch, Shearer was full of gratitude for everything Howe did throughout his four-and-a-half-year tenure at the club - referencing Newcastle's famous League Cup win against Liverpool last March.

'He gave me my best day as a Newcastle fan with that day at Wembley. He's given us some incredible nights in the Champions League that we'll never forget.

'He did a wonderful job for Newcastle, so it's a huge thank you to Eddie.'

Eddie Howe is waving goodbye to Newcastle after spending five years at the club

When Howe took over from Steve Bruce in November 2021, Newcastle were 19th in the league on four points after 10 matches. That season, he steered them to 11th with 49 points.

Since then, the Magpies have gone from strength to strength. On the rise, Shearer said: 'It's been an incredible ride. I think the job that he did was unbelievable from where he took us when he came, there was a real threat of relegation.

'He steadied the ship. He then got us climbing the league. He then brought in some wonderful players. He then took us to a final; we got beaten in that final, but then took us back again and gave us the day that we've so craved for.'

It's been widely reported that Al Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle will take over. The 38-year-old joined the Saudi outfit in 2023 and guided them to back-to-back AFC Champions League titles in 2024-25 and 2025-26.

Despite his impressive record in Saudi, Shearer believes it will be a challenge for him to follow Howe.

Alan Shearer has spoken of his surprise at seeing Howe leave the club during pre-season

'Clearly, he's got a great record in Saudi. Clearly, he's very young and inexperienced. The Premier League is a beast of a league. It's a big ask for anyone to come in and take over after what Eddie's done. If Jaissle does come in, you're asking a 38-year-old to navigate very, very tricky waters.'

In terms of what's next, the all-time Premier League top goalscorer has no doubts that Howe will have plenty of options.

'He won't be short of offers. We know that, for what he's done and what he's achieved at Newcastle. There's no doubt that he'll have people knocking on his door from all over the world. So we'll have to wait and see what is next for him.'

But for Newcastle, who have very limited time with their new boss before the Premier League gets underway, they need to find some stability quickly.

Shearer said: 'I'd like to see Newcastle sign players, because it's alright having this bold new look of going for young, hungry players who are 30 or 40 million pounds. But also, the Premier League is tough. You need some experienced heads in there as well.

'There's no doubt this season's going to be a tough one for Newcastle. You can't keep selling your best players in the hope that you're going to get to where you want to get to. What I would like is stability.'

Sports.title: 'I used to hate the water and cried before swimming lessons!': Meet 18-year-old sensation Filip Nowacki, the Jersey A-level student who beat his idol Adam Ramsay-Peaty
Sports.content:
During Filip Nowacki’s childhood, which was not all that long ago, his parents gave him an ultimatum.

‘Me and my friends would go out to Greve de Lecq, which is a popular beach where you can go cliff jumping,’ explains the 18-year-old from Jersey.

‘It’s a five-minute swim across to the rocks where you jump in. It’s maybe 15 metres high. It’s a bit hairy for a responsible adult but it’s a good adrenaline kick.

‘It’s very important you know how to swim so my parents wanted me to be able to keep myself afloat when I went out with my mates.’

When they doubled down on his swimming lessons, little did they know that Nowacki would be winning gold and silver medals at the 2026 Commonwealth Games.

The teenager, who is still waiting for his A-level results, has been Glasgow’s breakthrough star. He beat his idol, Adam Ramsay-Peaty, on Saturday night and has become one of swimming’s overnight sensations.

Teenager Filip Nowacki, who is still waiting for his A-level results, has been Glasgow’s breakthrough star after beating his idol, Adam Ramsay-Peaty, on Saturday night

Last year, after finishing his lower-sixth exams, he won the 200m breaststroke at the Junior European Championships with a time that would have medalled at the 2024 Olympics in Paris

Sitting in the team room in Glasgow, beaming ear to ear after his victory, Nowacki takes Daily Mail Sport through his journey to the podium.

His surname has Polish roots. In 2002, his mum and dad boarded a one-way flight to Jersey and landed jobs in accounting and construction.

‘They took me to swimming lessons when I was five or six and I hated it,’ he recalls. ‘I hated the water, I hated getting wet and I cried before I got in. When I was seven or eight, I started to enjoy it. I went for a trial taster session at Jersey swimming club and thought, “This is a bit of me”.

‘You’re never far from the sea in Jersey. You can go for open-water swims but I’ve never been the biggest, so I had to get my elbows out because of all the waves. I definitely preferred sticking to the black line of the pool.’

At secondary school, students were pushed to take part in all sports. One look at Nowacki’s slight 5ft 10in frame, however, will tell you that he was not destined for contact sports.

‘I played a bit of house rugby but I tended to run away from the ball!’ he laughs.

‘I did a lot of sports growing up, but mainly swimming, cycling and running. When I was 14, I went to the swimming nationals. It was at Ponds Forge in Sheffield and that really sparked my journey. I was between 10th and 20th in all events when I arrived and I walked away with four golds. That was my first experience of what it feels like to win.’

Nowacki has never looked back. His swimming coach at the Jersey Tigers convinced him to move to Millfield boarding school for his sixth form studies, where he could spend more time perfecting his technique.

Last year, after finishing his lower-sixth exams, he won the 200m breaststroke at the Junior European Championships with a time that would have medalled at the 2024 Olympics in Paris.

People talk about these games as a launchpad for greatness and his name is worth remembering for LA 2028

‘This is the first competition where I haven’t had maths or physics to worry about in the background,’ he explains. ‘I had all my A levels leading up to these Games, which was quite intense. I was spending a lot of time on my iPad reading over notes and making flash cards. Knowing I don’t have any schoolwork to do whilst I’ve been here has been quite nice!’

Nowacki has been staying in the same hotel as Ramsay-Peaty, overlooking the River Clyde. He is not blessed with his senior’s upper body strength – joking that maybe one day he will ‘get hench’.

While Ramsay-Peaty changed the game with his bulldog-like power, Nowacki is more like a skimming stone. ‘I saw Adam in the lift after my race on Tuesday night and he congratulated me. I’ve looked up to him for most of my life. I was eight years old when he won his first Olympic gold so to be racing in the lane next to him is pretty special.

‘We went for a coffee before the Commonwealth Games and I peppered him with questions for an hour and a half. I’m trying to draw as much experience from him as possible. Going up against some of those lads in the 100 breast can be a challenge because they’re so much bigger than me. I’m not the tallest of men and I’d love to put on muscle but there’s no point, given the momentum I’m carrying in the 200. If I get too big, I’m going to end up fighting the water, rather than gliding through it.’

Nowacki has been gliding through the Glaswegian waters with an effortless cadence. People talk about these games as a launchpad for greatness and his name is worth remembering for LA 2028.

‘Every athlete dreams of the Olympic Games,’ he says. ‘They are staging the swimming in a 40-thousand capacity arena which will be unreal. Coming here and winning medals is a big step in the right direction.’

'He's swimming times that have never been seen from an 18-year-old'

By Michael Jamieson, Olympic silver medallist and TNT Sports expert

Watching Filip Nowacki in the pool brings back memories of seeing Kosuke Kitajima win double gold for Japan at the 2004 and 2008 Olympics.

They’re both relatively small but they possess so much natural speed. Filip is swimming times that have never been seen from an 18-year-old so he’s a real trailblazer.

You don’t want to pile expectation onto his shoulders but he’s already right at the sharp end of the global rankings. There are Japanese and Chinese athletes who are swimming slightly faster times but Filip has just come out of juniors and he’s already right behind them.

He lined up against Adam Ramsay-Peaty in the 50 and 100m breaststroke this week and everyone has been comparing their physical appearance. They’re very different.

For me, Filip naturally set up as a 200m swimmer. Technically, he is absolutely perfect. He’s got a bit of a longer stroke, with a lower stroke rate. You can see the leg drive come in as his hands shoot forward. His streamline position is great and the timing is perfect. It’s a flawless cascade of movement patterns.

With some of the heavier guys, like Adam, you see their hips drop in the last 50m over four lengths. That’s when it becomes harder and harder for those heavier, muscly guys. Filip’s hips are high when he drives his legs and his body sits right on top of the water. He seems to have the perfect blend between speed, technique and timing. That’s married up with the fitness and endurance he has for the 200m.

'Watching Filip Nowacki in the pool brings back memories of seeing Kosuke Kitajima win double gold for Japan at the 2004 and 2008 Olympics,' says TNT Sports expert Jamieson

'He lined up against Adam Ramsay-Peaty in the 50 and 100m breaststroke and everyone has been comparing their physical appearance. They’re very different,' says Jamieson

He’s burst onto the scene over the last 12 months. He’s won junior titles and swam the 2.07 benchmark that sets apart the world class. Because he speaks so eloquently, I don’t think there was any doubt that he would be affected by the occasion of these Games.

The exciting thing is he has still got areas where he can improve. His muscle mass will increase as he develops towards the 2028 Olympics, where he should be in firm medal contention.

It’s a monumental step to win your first senior title immediately after your junior career. He’s going to emerge as the face of the men’s breaststroke scene and his support team need to manage that. He’s made it look so easy and that’s fantastic news for both Jersey and Great Britain.

Sports.title: Who is Matthias Jaissle? Newcastle's managerial target has won titles in Austria and Saudi Arabia, bases his style on the likes of Thomas Tuchel and Jurgen Klopp... but had no dreams of becoming a boss!
Sports.content:
Who is Matthias Jaissle? Newcastle's managerial target has won titles in Austria and Saudi Arabia, bases his style on the likes of Thomas Tuchel and Jurgen Klopp... but had no dreams of becoming a boss!

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Newcastle's summer of upheaval has continued with news that manager Eddie Howe is leaving.

The stunning news broke on Thursday morning and comes the morning after their 4-1 pre-season defeat at Championship side Bristol City.

With Howe's four-year and eight-month tenure coming to an end, Daily Mail Sport has detailed that Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle is the leading candidate for the role. Newcastle and Al-Ahli are both majority-owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund.

The 38-year-old German has held talks with the Newcastle hierarchy about succeeding Howe and has a track record of success despite his relative infancy into first-team management.

His first job only came in January 2021 when he was announced as head coach of Austrian second-tier side Liefering. With just a few months remaining of that campaign he guided them to second place - their joint-highest finish in their history.

That summer he replaced Jesse Marsch as manager of RB Salzburg and the 2021-22 campaign yielded success as he led the club to the domestic double of the Austrian Bundesliga and Austrian Cup titles. He also led the club to the Champions League knockout phase for the first time in their history.

Al-Ahli manager Matthias Jaissle is being lined up to replace Eddie Howe as Newcastle boss

Howe left his role as Newcastle boss on Thursday morning after four years and eight months

Jaissle backed up that silverware with more the following term as Salzburg were crowned Austrian league winners once more. However, he was sacked on the eve of the 2023-24 season with Al-Ahli becoming his next destination.

Joining the Saudi club on a three-year contract, his success has continued in the Middle East - with the club winning their first-ever Asian Champions League title in 2024-25 and repeating the feat this season - with the likes of Ivan Toney, Riyad Mahrez and Edouard Mendy in his side.

His managerial success is the more remarkable considering it is not a career he desired. Having come through Stuttgart's youth system under Thomas Tuchel, Jaissle was a promising young defender at Hoffenheim - who were managed by Ralf Rangnick - before injury befell him. In 2009, the Germany Under-21 international suffered an anterior cruciate ligament tear against Hannover and was never the same and eventually retired at 26 years old in 2014.

Reflecting on what could have been, he told Give Me Sport in December 2024: 'My knee injury was a shock. Probably the only advantage of it was that I could start management earlier.

'I am still young for a coach but have quite good experience already. I would still love to be playing, even at 36. I kick every ball when given the chance in training!

'I like to think I'd be in my last season now as a player if I was fit, but that's life, and I am grateful for the next chapter and the opportunities I have had so far.'

His pathway to management began when he was invited by Rangnick, then RB Leipzig's head of sport, onto a trainee programme within the club's youth department. The rest is now history.

Rangnick and Tuchel are two managers Jaissle looks up to as well as someone he could be facing in the opposition dugout next season in Tottenham counterpart Roberto De Zerbi: 'I have had quite a unique coaching path, eventually leading me here to the Al-Ahli job in Saudi Arabia,' he continued.

The 38-year-old German has won silverware at old side RB Salzburg (left) as well as at Al-Ahli

'I have always tried to be authentic as a coach and find my own way. Of course, I have influences. Ralf Rangnick played a big part in developing my ideas because I played under him for most of my playing career. And in my youth, I had Thomas Tuchel, so I have followed his principles and career.

'Then there's Jurgen Klopp - I often looked at the transitions he put in place with Liverpool. In possession, I like how Pep Guardiola finds structure and balance. And there's a lot to take from Roberto De Zerbi's build-up as well.

'It's a constant learning process. And in the next few years, I'm sure there will be a different coach to draw inspiration from. It's not about copying other coaches, it's just about being inspired by them.'

Speaking about his management philosophy to The Athletic in January, he said: 'I want stress on the opponent as soon as possible.

'And when we win the ball, I want to go as quickly as possible towards the opponent's goal. I'm very vertical in that approach.'

With key duo Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali having already departed, and with captain Bruno Guimaraes' future increasingly uncertain, Jaissle will have a big rebuild on his hands if he does swap Saudi for Tyneside.

Compatriots Thomas Tuchel (left) and Jurgen Klopp are among the influences on his tactics

And with all the turmoil going on at St James' Park, club legend Alan Shearer insists Jaissle will need time if he does take the job.

'It's being reported that Matthias Jaissle is set to come in. I think we have to be careful if that is the case not to pile on,' Shearer told Betfair.

'Clearly, he's got a great record in Saudi. Clearly, he's very young and inexperienced. The Premier League is a beast of a league. It's a big ask for anyone to come in and take over after what Eddie's done.

'I don't think it's a great look for what's happening at the minute with Newcastle, you know, it's like what's going on? We're selling all our best players. The fans are seeing [Alexander] Isak go, the fans are seeing Tonali go, the fans are seeing Gordon go.

'My guess is it's probably only a matter of time before Bruno goes, because he'll look at what's happening with all those players and look at what's happening with Eddie and think, 'Well, from a personal point of view, from his point of view, I guess I'm going to be next.

'It's certainly not a good look, and they'll have to navigate some tough waves coming their way now, because it's the unknown. I mean, if Jaissle does come in, you're asking a 38-year-old to come in and navigate very, very tricky waters.'

Buckle up, Newcastle fans, whatever happens.
